The Department of Statistics and the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences (EECS) at the University of California, Berkeley, invite applications for a joint tenure-track position at the Assistant Professor level. This position is expected to be 50% time in each of the Departments of EECS and Statistics, although an appointment at different percentages can be made by mutual agreement.
  
This position aims to build upon Berkeley's legacy at the intersection of statistics and computer science in the areas of Machine Learning (ML) and Artificial Intelligence (AI). We seek exceptional candidates who will expand our strength in shared research areas of critical need, Trustworthy AI and Foundations of Statistical ML and AI, while supporting undergraduate and graduate teaching in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (AI/ML).

The Berkeley Department of Statistics is part of the College of Computing, Data Science, and Society (CDSS). It is consistently ranked as a top program in Statistics internationally. Since the inception of the Department in 1955, graduates and faculty of Berkeley have shaped the foundations and applications of Statistics, Data Science, and Machine Learning. The department is proud of our interdisciplinary and collaborative nature, with many faculty and students collaborating across fields such as biomedicine, public health, neuroscience, physical sciences, the social sciences, and computer science.

The EECS department is part of the College of Engineering (COE) and the College of Computing, Data Science, and Society (CDSS). It offers one of the strongest research and instructional programs in this field anywhere in the world. Our key strength is our array of cross-disciplinary, team-driven projects. The integration of EE and CS forms the core, with strong interactions that extend into many other disciplines.

jobs.title: Faculty Appointment, Religious Studies
jobs.description:
LaGrange College seeks to fill a tenure-track position at the assistant professor level in Religious Studies beginning August 1, 2027. The field of specialization is open, but preference will be given to candidates who can teach Christian ethics and broader philosophical approaches to ethics including Bioethics and possibly business ethics and the ethics of AI, as well as candidates prepared to contribute in areas such as American Christianity or world religious traditions.
  
  
A Ph.D. in religious studies or related field is required, although outstanding ABD candidates will be considered. The successful candidate must have their terminal degree completed prior to the end of their second year in the position.
  
  
The teaching load is four (4) courses per semester, including introductory courses, upper-level electives in the candidate’s field(s) of specialization, and courses that satisfy the college’s general education curriculum, known as Ethos. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to help shape the future of the major in religion and help create interdisciplinary approaches to critical analyses of American culture and society. The position includes the supervision and mentorship of undergraduate research projects in the field. Candidates should demonstrate a commitment to excellence in teaching, professional development, and institutional service, as well as an understanding of, and appreciation for, the mission of liberal arts institutions.
  
  
The religion program maintains a close relationship with the Candler School of Theology at Emory University; students interested in a future ministry career will find a direct and accelerated pathway from LaGrange College to the Candler School of Theology. Through both a solid grounding in theory and engagement in the field (via internships, collaborative undergraduate research, and other opportunities) Religious Studies students receive a thorough, intensive, and experiential education in the discipline. The program’s historic engagement in LaGrange College’s undergraduate research program affords students the opportunity to work directly with faculty on research projects that build their professional skills. The college values its relationship with the United Methodist Church and in particular its commitment to the Wesleyan ideal of service.
  
  
Interested candidates should visit https://lagrangecollege.applicantstack.com/x/openings to apply for the position and to view other positions available at the college. Required documents include:
  
  

* A letter of interest describing the alignment of the candidate’s qualifications with the position requirements
* Current curriculum vitae
* A statement of teaching philosophy that also addresses ways in which the candidate creates and sustains a culture of belonging, fairness and appreciation for different perspectives in the classroom
* A statement of scholarly interests
* Graduate and undergraduate transcripts (copies are fine at this point)
* Contact information (only) for three professional references

Review of applications will begin Nov. 9 and will continue until the position is filled.
  
  
LaGrange College is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, sex, age, national origin, disability, veteran status or any other legally protected status.

**Job Title**

Director of Band & Instrumental Activities

**Agency**

East Texas A&M University

**Department**

Music

**Proposed Minimum Salary**

Commensurate

**Job Location**

Commerce, Texas

**Job Type**

Faculty

**Job Description**

**INSTRUCTIONS TO APPLICANT****:**

During the application process the *“My Experience*” page has a section provided “*Attachments (Resume/CV, References, Cover letter, etc.)*” to upload required documents.

* Use the Upload button to add each document.
* You will be able to upload up to 5 documents. Be aware that the maximum size allowed for any one document is 5MB.
* All documents must be electronically submitted through the Texas A&M Online Employment Services website to be considered.
* Incomplete or improperly submitted applications may be excluded from consideration.
* Please do not withdraw your application in an attempt to upload a missing document, instead please email HR for help.

**Please provide the following documents**:

* Cover Letter
* Curriculum vitae
* Selected repertoire list from the last five years
* A brief (one page) statement of teaching philosophy
* A brief (one page) statement of professional activity and goals (research and/or performance)
* Transcripts (unofficial and scanned copies are acceptable)
* The names and contact information for three professional references (at least one must be able to address teaching experience and teaching effectiveness; please indicate the teaching reference in your letter of application).
* At this time, please only upload the required documents listed above; semi-finalists may be asked to submit video recordings of their conducting in performance and rehearsal, and/or teaching.

If you need assistance, please contact us at HR.Hiring@etamu.edu

***A Presidential proclamation issued on September 19, 2025, imposes a $100,000 fee on new H-1B petitions filed after September 21, 2025. Please be advised that Texas A&M University will NOT pay this fee. Therefore, if you need immigration sponsorship for your employment, we recommend that you consult with your private immigration counsel at your own expense to ascertain whether your current immigration status would make a potential offer of employment from Texas A&M University subject to this fee.***

***In addition, on January 27, 2026, Texas Governor Abbot issued a moratorium on the filing of any new H-1B unless approved by the Texas Workforce Commission. Accordingly, if you will now or in the future require sponsorship for employment visa status this moratorium may affect our ability to employ you should you be selected as the final candidate.***

**SUMMARY:**

The School of Music at East Texas A&M invites applicants for a full-time, tenure-track Assistant/Associate Professor in Music (Director of Bands and Instrumental Activities). The successful candidate will provide artistic, academic, and programmatic leadership for the University's band program while contributing to teaching, Research, Scholarship, and Creative Activities (RSCA), recruitment, outreach, and service. The position includes a reduced teaching load to accommodate administrative duties, in consultation annually with the Director of the School of Music.

The School of Music at East Texas A&M serves approximately 240 music majors across instrumental, vocal, and keyboard areas and is fully accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM). It offers baccalaureate and master's degrees in music education and performance, and a Bachelor of Arts in Music. The School of Music is housed in a $30 million music building completed in 2010 containing state-of-the-art recital and concert halls, studios, rehearsal halls, classrooms, and teaching areas.

The band program includes three concert bands, two jazz ensembles, and marching and athletic bands. The Wind Ensemble has performed at both regional and national College Band Directors National Association Conferences as well as the Texas Music Educators Association Clinic/Convention, most recently in 2018. The Wind Ensemble is also actively involved in commissioning and premiering new works from the nation’s leading composers. The Marching Band performs at all home games as well as exhibitions at marching contests such as the Texas State UIL Marching Band Contest and Bands of America Regionals and Grand Nationals Marching Festival.

**DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Conduct the Wind Ensemble (top ensemble)
* Teach Graduate and Undergraduate Conducting
* Teach graduate coursework in instrumental repertoire and pedagogy
* Teach additional courses based upon the candidate’s area of expertise
* Organize and administer a comprehensive university band program including concert ensembles, marching band, jazz ensembles and athletic bands
* Provide overall leadership of the band staff and instrumental faculty, as well as program development
* Supervise budget management and fiscal responsibilities for division needs
* Recruit for the band and university at the regional and state level
* Promote the band and university at regional, state and national events
* Participate in creative and/or research activities consistent with all faculty appointments
* Participate in service activities consistent with all faculty appointments
* Other duties as assigned by the Director of the School of Music
* Participate in service activities consistent with all faculty appointments

**MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:**

* **Education:** Doctorate in Music Education, Conducting, or a closely related field from an accredited institution; equivalent university experience and demonstrated achievement maybe considered in lieu of the doctorate
* **Experience / Knowledge / Skills:** At least three (3) years of experience as either a Director or Assistant Director of Bands at the university level
* **Ability to:** Multi-task and work well as part of a team, manage budgets associated with an R2 institution, coordinate department-wide recruiting activities

**PREFERRED EDUCATION / SKILLS/ EXPERIENCE:**

* At least five (5) years of experience in university teaching

**APPLICATION REQUIREMENTS****:**

* Letter of application that addresses the position qualifications
* Curriculum vitae
* Selected repertoire list from the last five years
* A brief (one page) statement of teaching philosophy
* A brief (one page) statement of professional activity and goals (research and/or performance)
* Transcripts (unofficial and scanned copies are acceptable)
* The names and contact information for three professional references (at least one must be able to address teaching experience and teaching effectiveness; please indicate the teaching reference in your letter of application).
* At this time, please only upload the required documents listed above; semi-finalists may be asked to submit video recordings of their conducting in performance and rehearsal, and/or teaching.

**Review of candidates will begin on November 2nd, 2026.**

All positions are security-sensitive. Applicants are subject to a criminal history investigation, and employment is contingent upon the institution’s verification of credentials and/or other information required by the institution’s procedures, including the completion of the criminal history check.

Equal Opportunity/Veterans/Disability Employer.

Join a forward-thinking academic team shaping the future of healthcare education. As an Adjunct Faculty Member in the Doctor of Medical Science (DMSc) program, you will engage and mentor advanced practitioners through a dynamic, clinically relevant curriculum designed to elevate leadership and practice. We welcome candidates based in Iowa, as well as those in Wisconsin, Illinois, Missouri, and Indiana, who are committed to developing the next generation of healthcare professionals through high-quality, student-centered instruction.
  
  
**What You’ll Do**

* Teach and/or coordinate courses in the online Doctor of Medical Science program related to area of content expertise. Teaching courses includes preparation of the syllabus, preparation of learning materials, frequent and clear communication with students and other program faculty, strong faculty engagement and presence in the online course, and responsiveness to student questions (via email or in the course site)
* Seek and evaluate innovative educational methodologies to improve teaching and learning activities.
* Create or modify course content, assessments, and/or teaching style based on assessment results, professional development experience, and curricular mapping results.
* Participate in instructor evaluation, assessment of student academic achievement and demonstrate modification of teaching techniques in accordance with assessment feedback.
* Participate in program accreditation activities as assigned.
* Participate in and successfully complete all university-required training.
* Perform other job-related duties and special projects as assigned.

**What We Are Looking For**

* Faculty should hold the appropriate graduate degree, (e.g., DMSc, DHS, PhD, EdD, etc.) in physician assistant/associate, public health, health administration, or education or a closely related discipline relevant to the department’s academic curricula.
* Must be familiar with innovative teaching methodologies and effective student evaluation methods.
* Candidates located in Iowa are preferred; however, applicants from Wisconsin, Illinois, Missouri, or Indiana may also be considered.
* To see the full job description go to Position Description at the bottom of this posting.

**About**
Founded in 1898, Des Moines University is a premier medical and health sciences institution comprising three colleges– College of Osteopathic Medicine, College of Podiatric Medicine and Surgery, and College of Health Sciences – offering ten graduate degree programs.
  
  
Our mission is to improve lives in our global community by educating diverse groups of highly competent and compassionate health professionals.
  
  
It is an exciting time to join DMU. In 2023, we relocated our primary academic and operational offices to a new 88-acre campus in West Des Moines, Iowa, while maintaining an active clinic on our former campus. This state-of-the-art campus includes technology-rich, flexible education spaces that support innovative teaching methods and connect faculty and students across all of our programs. Our new research facilities include a vibrant and spacious open laboratory, designed to foster collaboration and innovation.
  
  
DMU enhances our community’s quality of life by educating outstanding health professionals and leaders; providing expert, compassionate patient care; serving the community in diverse ways; and stimulating the central Iowa community.
  
  
At DMU you will make a meaningful contribution to the dynamic future of Medicine and Health Sciences by supporting a diverse community of faculty and staff with programs and services across the employee lifecycle.
  
  
**Required Documents**
Resume, cover letter, and contact information for three professional references required at time of online submission. Apply at www.dmu.edu/employment.

**Job Description**
The Department of Anesthesiology at SUNY Downstate Health Sciences University is seeking a full-time Professor & Chair. Reporting to the Dean of the College of Medicine, the successful candidate will:
  
  

* Recruit, direct, and develop a faculty who, as a group, can provide the full range of anesthesia services, which includes:

+ 20 full-time clinical faculty that care for patients at University Hospital at Downstate and the ambulatory surgery unit at Kings County Hospital Center
+ A 4-year accredited Residency Program with 17 Residents at each training level
+ The College of Medicine Anesthesiology Clerkship with approximately 10 students per each two-week rotation

* Be responsible for administrative operations of the academic Department of Anesthesiology in the College of Medicine.
* Be responsible for the oversight and success of the academic mission of the department and its faculty throughout the DHSU academic system, including its teaching enterprise in medical student education (UME), resident education (GME), and Continuing Medical Education (CME), as well as the department's research enterprise.
* Work with leadership of University Hospital at Downstate and its affiliated teaching hospitals (which include Kings County Hospital Center, Maimonides Medical Center, the Brooklyn Veteran's Administration Medical Center, and One Brooklyn Health) and with the Clinical Practice Management Plan (Downstate Health Physicians), the Chair will be responsible for oversight of the academic programs and the associated clinical enterprise.
* Endeavor to advance faculty development in clinical and academic skills within the department and throughout the entire network.
* Act in concert with the Chair of the Department of Surgery in providing oversight of the Operating Rooms, and in working to improve the efficiency of Perioperative Services.
* Lead the faculty (both current and those recruited) at all sites in the development of innovative clinical and basic research initiatives, either independently or in collaboration with other investigators on our faculty, other schools, and community organizations. A reputation for path-breaking research will, in turn, enhance our ability to attract patients, referrals, and residents, creating the foundation for a new phase of departmental growth. It is expected that the faculty the Chair will recruit will significantly expand the range of services available to its patients while providing a superb educational experience for our residents and students.
* Maintain and enhance Downstate's residency program and our clerkship offering for medical students. Our graduates have long been recognized as being well prepared to make significant contributions in their discipline, but we believe that we can further enhance the quality and reputation of these programs and will rely on the Chair and the faculty to devote considerable attention to this task. Together with Downstate's academic partners, these programs will prepare the next generation of leaders and practitioners in this field for careers in Brooklyn, New York City, and the nation, and carve a place for Downstate as a leading center for state­ of-the-art anesthesiology services.
* Have the demonstrated capacity to foster an environment in which excellence in teaching, research and scholarship flourish, as well as experience in developing and leading clinical, educational and research programs. Candidates must have a record of effective administrative and fiscal leadership, national stature in academic Anesthesiology, demonstrated experience promoting a diverse workforce, excellent interpersonal skills, and positive interactions with faculty, students, and staff.

**Qualifications**

* Medical Doctor Degree.
* New York State Medical Licensure.
* Board certified in Anesthesiology.

jobs.title: Adjunct Professor - CSPP: Clinical PsyD Program- San Diego Campus Candidate Pool
jobs.description:
The Clinical PSYD Program in San Diego follows a Practitioner-Scholar model that emphasizes the applications of theory and research to clinical practice. The program develops competent professional health-care psychologists skilled in delivering a variety of clinical services to diverse populations in varied settings. The program’s most distinctive component is its dual emphasis on clinical expertise and clinical scholarship. Students take courses in a wide range of subjects, including statistics, theories of personality, psychological assessment, multicultural issues, and psychological practice. Students may follow their own clinical interests and further their individual career goals by selecting a specialized series of courses, research, and field placements related to a particular area of practice.

**Application Description:**

Applicants to this position will be considered for a candidate pool encompassing one or more of the subject areas outlined in the job description. This pool will be used to identify qualified candidates for potential appointments during the 2026–2027 academic year.

**Salary Range:**
$39 - $46 hourly (based on course requirements & level of education). This is a temporary, non-benefits eligible role.

Qualifications

**Minimum Requirements:**

* **Education:**
  Doctoral or other terminal degree in Psychology or associated field, from an accredited college or university.
* **Experience:**
  Appropriate experience in the areas(s) of specialization and expertise
* **Certifications, Licenses, etc.:**
  Clinical Psychology license required for clinical courses.

Additional Information

**Specific Courses:**

**Fall 2026 (Aug. 17, 2026 – Dec. 20, 2026)**

**PSY60300 Advanced Statistics**

The objective of this 3-unit course is to understand applied research methodology, evaluate and synthesize psychological research literature, and apply both to clinical challenges. The course will provide an overview of the major statistical tools employed in contemporary behavioral science research and program evaluation. Topics surveyed will be the philosophy of science and scientific method; descriptive and inferential statistics; univariate and multivariate analysis of variance and co-variance (one-way and factorial); regression techniques; principal and (exploratory and confirmatory) factor analysis; power calculation and corrections for multiple comparisons.

**Spring 2027 (Jan 4, 2027 – May 16, 2027)**

**PSY61122 Social Basis of Behavior**

This 2-unit course will enable students to develop competence and understanding of clinical implications with respect to:

* The social development of the self (e.g., self-perception and self-efficacy).
* Interpersonal relations (e.g., attraction, love, and marriage).
* Attitude formation and change; aggression.
* Social influences (e.g., conformity, obedience).
* Attribution and social cognition.
* Group behavior and performance.
* Culture, prejudice and stigma.



**PSY65400 Family Systems Theory**

This 2-unit course will prepare students to be effective professional therapists who have increased awareness in the following areas:

* Overviews of the theories of family therapy and evidence based principles.
* Practical applications of Family Systems Theory.
* Connection between Family Systems Theory and clinical practice.
* Social, cultural, political and economic issues and contexts in Family Therapy.
* Develop knowledge of the assessment, diagnosis, and treatment planning as related to Family Systems Theory.

**PSY61050 Biological Aspects of Behavior**

This 3-unit course is designed to provide the graduate student in psychology with a comprehensive overview of the field of biological psychology. The purpose of the course is for students:

* To develop an understanding of the research results, research methodology, and techniques of data collection/analysis in the area of biological psychology.
* To demonstrate intermediate knowledge the core areas of biological psychology.
* To display critical scientific thinking in the area of biological psychology.
* To develop the ability to review, evaluate, and synthesize biological psychology research.
* To utilize this theoretical and scientific knowledge as a basis for the effective practice of clinical psychology.

**PSY61402 Developmental Psychology**

This two-unit course for second year Psy.D. students covers a wide range of developmental stages and topics including both adaptive and challenging developmental pathways. The course includes a study of developmental theories, psychopathology, constructs, research and research methods as they contribute to an understanding of normal human development and its variants. Psychological development from conception through aging and death are covered. Contemporary issues and trends are discussed. All areas of development covered in this course will be studied and considered within appropriate cultural contexts.

Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

* Compare and contrast numerous theories of physical, cognitive and social/emotional development.
* Apply research and theories of development across the lifespan within a broad social and cultural context.
* Acquire knowledge to think critically about varying development trajectories when determining adaptive and maladaptive
* developmental pathways.
* More fully understand how their life experiences and own development influence their understanding of human development.



**PSY65030 Personality Assessment I**

The purpose of this 3 unit course is to subject students to a wide variety of the most widely utilized personality instruments in psychology today and to learn how to generate a psychological report that is accurate, supportive and has the potential to change the patient’s trajectory. Following the course on Intellectual Assessment students completing PSY 6503- Personality Assessment I will be subjected to, and demonstrate mastery of the following personality assessment components:

**History of personality assessment.**

The development of various significant personality assessment instruments.

Proper test selection for adults and children as well as referral question.

How to write a detailed, accurate, and compassionate psychological report.

How to develop a diagnosis with the aid of personality test data.

How to develop meaningful recommendations from personality test data.

**PSY60140 Qualitative Methods of Research**

The purpose of this 3-unit course is to subject students to a wide variety of the most widely utilized personality instruments in psychology today and to learn how to generate a psychological report that is accurate, supportive and has the potential to change the patient’s trajectory. Following the course on Intellectual Assessment students completing PSY 6503- Personality Assessment I will be subjected to, and demonstrate mastery of the following personality assessment components:

**History of personality assessment**

The development of various significant personality assessment instruments

Proper test selection for adults and children as well as referral question

How to write a detailed, accurate, and compassionate psychological report

How to develop a diagnosis with the aid of personality test data

How to develop meaningful recommendations from personality test data

**PSY60310 Statistics, Psychometrics, and Research Design**

This 3-unit course is designed to prepare students to achieve graduate-level knowledge in the discipline-specific knowledge areas of Research Methods, Statistical Analysis, and Psychometrics and the profession-wide competency of Research. The goal of this course is an understanding of the principles and methods of psychological research, which will include areas of hypothesis testing, experimental design options, sample selection, control group strategies, criteria and criterion measures, psychometrics, data analysis, and interpretation of results. The course will enable students to understand how research is properly done and to discriminate between adequate and inadequate research conclusions. The pros and cons of experimental versus nonexperimental research will be examined, and those of quantitative versus qualitative research, among other issues. This training should prepare students to become enlightened consumers as well as potential producers of research and for the application of research methods to program evaluation

**Duties & Responsibilities:**

* Facilitating Classroom and Distance/Distributed Learning.
* Course and syllabus preparation.
* Class curriculum coordination and planning.
* Assessment and evaluation of learners.
* Mentoring and advising students.
* Holding office hours and meeting with students.
* Research/scholarship mentoring and supervision.

**Skills:**

* Proficient computer skills, including proficiency with Microsoft Office programs.
* The ability to work independently and be self-motivated.
* High level of accuracy and attention to detail and the ability to problem solve.
* The ability to explain complex requirements in clear and concise terms.
* The ability to be flexible with workflow to meet the needs of the department and students and to manage multiple tasks per required deadlines.
* The drive to encourage, direct, hold accountable and guide candidates toward task completion.

Hiring Department
  
  
College of Nursing, UMSL
  
  
**Job Description**
The College of Nursing is excited to welcome a new Assistant Professor, tenure track, who has high potential for growth through their research, teaching, and service. Tenure-track faculty are expected to establish or maintain a sustained, extramurally funded program of research, disseminate scholarly works in high-impact, peer-reviewed journals, and deliver exceptional, evidence-based instruction. Teaching assignments are balanced against research productivity. This individual will meaningfully contribute to College, University, professional, and community through service.
  
  
**Responsibilities And Essential Functions**
**Research & Scholarship**

* Establish and maintain a sustainable, identifiable program of research that expands the body of nursing knowledge.
* Demonstrate a sustained record of seeking competitive funding (intramural and extramural) to advance their specific research agenda.
* Disseminate research findings via peer reviewed data-based journal articles and presentations at regional, national, and international scientific conferences.

**Teaching, Mentorship, and Educational Leadership**

* Deliver excellent instruction in undergraduate and/or graduate programs based on areas of expertise, adapting to varying course complexities and enrollment sizes. (Instructional workload is subject to departmental allocation and external funding buyouts).
* Employ innovative, inclusive pedagogical methods, educational technologies (e.g., simulation, telehealth tools), or curriculum re-designs that educate students, colleagues, patients, or communities from a wide range of backgrounds and experiences.
* Participate actively in course and program meetings to contribute to the ongoing development, continuous evaluation, and enhancement of academic programs.
* Support graduate and undergraduate student milestones by participating on PhD dissertation and DNP project committees, and mentoring students through research engagement and scholarly dissemination.

**Service & Professional Citizenship**

* Maintain a dependable institutional service record, taking on meaningful governance responsibilities within the College of Nursing that grow over time.
* Establish growing engagement with professional nursing organizations, scientific societies, or specialty bodies at the local, regional, and national levels, including participation in the peer-review process for professional journals.

**Qualifications**
**Minimum Qualifications:**

* Holds a PhD in Nursing or a health-related field. \*Will consider an all but dissertation PhD candidate with degree conferral prior to faculty appointment.
* An emerging body of research that aligns with a PhD dissertation or previous work experience.
* Current nursing license, without restriction, to practice nursing, and eligibility for RN licensure in Missouri

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Prior experience or active training in submitting proposals to federal funding agencies (e.g., NIH/NINR, HRSA, CDC) or foundations.
* Demonstrated commitment to advancing health for all people and the development of leaders from varied backgrounds.
* Experience with teaching across programs (undergraduate and graduate) including in-person didactic and clinical lab as well as online education with strong technology skills.
* A clearly articulated and focused trajectory of research demonstrating potential for long-term sustainability and intellectual independence as evidenced by peer-reviewed publications and/or a demonstrated readiness or record of seeking competitive external grant funding.

This list of qualifications is intended to inform prospective candidates of the factors upon which their candidacies will be evaluated. The absence of one or more of these factors will not necessarily cause a candidate to be removed from consideration or potential appointment.
  
  
Application Materials
  
  
Application materials should include a letter of interest, curriculum vita, and a philosophy of research, teaching and service.
  
  
Application Deadline
  
  
Applications will be reviewed beginning September 22 but will be accepted until the position is filled.
  
  
Sponsorship Information
  
  
Employment visa sponsorship may be available for candidates currently in the United States in H-1B status or other work-authorized status.
  
  
Benefit Eligibility
  
  
This position is eligible for University benefits. As part of your total compensation, the University offers a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental and vision plans, retirement, and educational fee discounts for all four UM System campuses. For additional information on University benefits, please visit the Faculty & Staff Benefits website at https://www.umsystem.edu/departments-staff/human-resources/benefits-retirement

The University of Missouri is an Equal Opportunity Employer.
  
  
To request ADA accommodations, please email the Office of Human Resources at umslhr@umsl.edu.

jobs.title: Faculty, Doctor of Executive Leadership (DEL)
jobs.description:
**Description**
**About Arkansas Colleges of Health Education**
Arkansas Colleges of Health Education (ACHE) is a private, non-profit, graduate-level health sciences institution located on over 500 acres in Fort Smith, Arkansas. ACHE’s service-driven mission is to educate and train a diverse group of competent and compassionate healthcare professionals; to create health and research support facilities; and to provide healthy living environments to improve the lives of others. Founded in 2014, ACHE has experienced rapid growth and is poised to be a leader in healthcare education for years to come. ACHE is the first and only private institution in Arkansas that is dedicated solely to healthcare and wellness, and maintains a strong commitment to the surrounding community.
  
  
**About Fort Smith And The Arkansas River Valley**
Fort Smith is a vibrant community of around 90,000, with a low cost of living and ample recreational opportunities. Located in the beautiful Arkansas River Valley at the foothills of the Ozark mountains, Fort Smith is nestled between the Ozark-St. Francis and Ouachita National Forests. The region provides hiking, mountain biking, rock climbing, hang gliding, whitewater rafting, and camping all within a short drive. In addition, the city supports a variety of cultural attractions, including museums, theaters, an award-winning symphony, and two historic entertainment districts.
  
  
**LOCATION**
This is a hybrid position. The employee will be remote the majority of the time, with the supervisor determining any residential requirements.
  
  
**Job Summary**
The Doctor of Executive Leadership (DEL) Faculty member is a collaborative educator and scholar committed to excellence in graduate education, executive leadership development, scholarship, service, and continuous program improvement.
  
  
The faculty member will contribute to the delivery and ongoing development of the Doctor of Executive Leadership program through high-quality online instruction, curriculum development, student advising and mentorship, scholarly activity, program assessment, and institutional and professional service.
  
  
The faculty member will work collaboratively with the DEL Program Director, faculty, staff, students, and institutional leadership to support the mission, vision, goals, and continued growth of the DEL program and Arkansas Colleges of Health Education (ACHE).
  
  
The faculty member will carry a teaching load as assigned based on program needs and institutional expectations and will actively contribute to the academic, scholarly, and service missions of ACHE.
  
  
**Essential Functions And Responsibilities**
**Teaching and Curriculum**

* Teach online Doctor of Executive Leadership courses within areas of demonstrated academic or professional competence.
* Provide high-quality, engaging, doctoral-level instruction appropriate for experienced working professionals and executive leaders.
* Develop, review, and revise course content, instructional materials, learning activities, and assessments.
* Ensure alignment among course learning outcomes, program learning outcomes, instructional activities, and assessments.
* Maintain current, evidence-informed course content reflecting contemporary leadership theory, organizational practice, healthcare, business, policy, and other relevant areas.
* Utilize effective online teaching methodologies and educational technologies to promote student engagement and learning.
* Provide timely, substantive, and constructive feedback on student assignments and academic performance.
* Maintain consistent course organization, communication, grading practices, and academic expectations.
* Participate in continuous curriculum review and improvement.
* Support the development of new DEL courses, concentrations, certificates, educational pathways, and other curricular initiatives as assigned.
* Maintain the security and integrity of course materials, assessments, student information, and academic records.
* Teach courses in other ACHE programs when appropriate based on expertise and institutional needs.

**Student Advising and Mentorship**

* Serve as an academic advisor and mentor to DEL students as assigned.
* Maintain appropriate availability and responsiveness to students.
* Monitor student academic progression and provide guidance when academic or professional development needs are identified.
* Provide individualized mentorship that connects doctoral education with students' professional leadership goals and organizational impact.
* Support students experiencing academic difficulty and participate in remediation activities when appropriate.
* Refer student concerns involving academic performance, professionalism, or conduct to the DEL Program Director in accordance with institutional policies.
* Support student scholarly activities, presentations, publications, professional development, and other academic opportunities.
* Promote a supportive, inclusive, professional, and academically rigorous learning environment.

**Scholarship and Research**

* Maintain an active program of scholarship appropriate to academic rank, professional expertise, and institutional expectations.
* Engage in research, applied scholarship, scholarly writing, peer-reviewed publication, professional presentations, or other recognized forms of scholarly activity.
* Pursue opportunities for collaborative scholarship with DEL faculty, ACHE faculty, students, and external partners.
* Mentor DEL students in scholarly inquiry, evidence-based leadership, research, and dissemination of scholarly work when appropriate.
* Participate in the development and evaluation of DEL program-related research and scholarly initiatives.
* Seek opportunities to translate research and professional experience into knowledge that advances executive leadership, organizational performance, healthcare, education, or other relevant fields.
* Pursue external funding, grants, or collaborative research opportunities when appropriate.
* Disseminate scholarly work at local, state, national, and international professional forums.

**Program Assessment and Continuous Improvement**

* Participate in the ongoing assessment and evaluation of the DEL curriculum and program.
* Assist with evaluation of course learning outcomes, program learning outcomes, student performance, and other measures of program effectiveness.
* Participate in the collection, analysis, and interpretation of assessment data.
* Contribute to accreditation, institutional effectiveness, and continuous quality-improvement activities as assigned.
* Participate in periodic review and revision of course materials, curriculum, academic policies, and program processes.
* Provide recommendations to the DEL Program Director regarding opportunities to improve academic quality, student outcomes, and program effectiveness.
* Maintain required academic and administrative documentation in accordance with ACHE policies and applicable accreditation standards

**Program and Institutional Service**

* Serve as a member of DEL program committees and other ACHE committees as assigned.
* Participate in faculty meetings, curriculum meetings, assessment activities, retreats, and other institutional responsibilities.
* Participate in DEL admissions activities, including applicant review, interviews, and candidate evaluation as requested.
* Support DEL orientation, information sessions, recruitment events, student activities, and other program initiatives.
* Participate in faculty governance and institutional service activities consistent with academic appointment and institutional expectations.
* Collaborate with faculty and staff across ACHE programs to advance interdisciplinary education and institutional initiatives.
* Support the mission, vision, values, and strategic priorities of ACHE.
* Participate in commencement, academic ceremonies, institutional events, and other activities requiring faculty representation as appropriate.

**Recruitment and Program Growth**

* Support recruitment and enrollment initiatives for the DEL program.
* Participate in information sessions, webinars, conferences, professional meetings, and other recruitment activities as requested.
* Engage professional networks and organizations to increase awareness of the DEL program.
* Identify opportunities for educational partnerships, professional collaborations, and student recruitment.
* Support development of relationships with healthcare systems, academic institutions, professional organizations, government agencies, military organizations, nonprofit organizations, and other potential partners when appropriate.
* Assist in identifying emerging leadership-development needs and opportunities that may inform future DEL curriculum and program growth.

**Professional and External Engagement**

* Maintain active engagement within relevant professional and academic communities.
* Represent ACHE and the DEL program professionally at conferences, meetings, educational events, and community activities.
* Participate in local, state, regional, national, or international professional service appropriate to expertise and academic role.
* Develop relationships that may contribute to educational opportunities, research, scholarship, student development, or institutional partnerships.
* Maintain professional competence and remain current within areas of academic and professional expertise.

**Faculty Responsibilities And Professional Conduct**

* Maintain professional, ethical, and collegial relationships with students, faculty, staff, institutional leadership, and external partners.
* Demonstrate reliability, accountability, professionalism, and responsiveness in fulfilling assigned responsibilities.
* Adhere to ACHE policies and procedures and applicable academic, regulatory, accreditation, and ethical standards.
* Maintain confidentiality and privacy of student, faculty, and institutional information.
* Demonstrate respect for diverse perspectives, backgrounds, professional experiences, and areas of expertise.
* Contribute to a collaborative, solutions-focused, and professional faculty environment.
* Participate in faculty development and continuing professional education as appropriate.
* Complete required institutional training and administrative responsibilities in a timely manner.
* Perform other duties as assigned by the DEL Program Director, Dean, or their designee.

**Teaching Load**

* The DEL Faculty member will carry a teaching load as determined by the DEL Program Director and institutional leadership based on program needs, faculty workload expectations, areas of expertise, and other assigned responsibilities.
* Teaching assignments may include DEL courses as well as courses in other ACHE academic programs when appropriate, based on faculty expertise and institutional needs.
* Perform other duties as assigned by the Program Director, Doctor of Executive Leadership or their designee.

**Requirements**
**QUALIFICATIONS AND CREDENTIALS**
**Education And Experience**
**Minimum Qualifications**

* Earned doctoral degree from an appropriately accredited institution in leadership, healthcare, business, education, organizational leadership, public administration, or another field relevant to the DEL curriculum.
* Credentials sufficient to qualify for academic appointment at the level of Assistant Professor or higher.
* Demonstrated experience in higher education, professional education, executive education, or a related academic environment.
* Demonstrated experience in leadership, administration, organizational management, healthcare, education, business, government, military leadership, or another area relevant to the DEL curriculum.
* Experience developing, managing, or teaching online or technology-enhanced curriculum.
* Evidence of commitment to excellence in teaching, scholarship, service, and student mentorship.
* Ability to contribute to doctoral-level education for experienced professionals and executive leaders.
* Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with faculty, staff, students, and institutional leadership.
* Strong written, verbal, interpersonal, organizational, and professional communication skills.
* Commitment to the mission, vision, and values of ACHE.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Significant progressive leadership or executive experience.
* Experience teaching at the doctoral or graduate level.
* Experience developing or delivering online doctoral education.
* Experience mentoring doctoral or graduate students.
* Record of peer-reviewed scholarship, professional presentations, applied research, or other scholarly activity.
* Experience with curriculum development, program assessment, accreditation, or institutional effectiveness.
* Experience working across disciplines or within complex organizations.
* Experience developing external partnerships, professional collaborations, or funded projects.
* Demonstrated national or international professional engagement within an area relevant to the DEL program.

**Required Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities**

* Ability to provide high-quality doctoral-level instruction in an online learning environment.
* Ability to effectively mentor and advise experienced professionals and executive-level students.
* Ability to translate theory, research, and evidence into practical leadership and organizational applications.
* Ability to critically analyze complex organizational and leadership challenges.
* Ability to design and evaluate graduate-level learning activities and assessments.
* Strong organizational and time-management skills with the ability to manage multiple responsibilities and priorities.
* Ability to work independently while functioning effectively as part of a collaborative academic team.
* Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
* Ability to effectively use learning management systems, Microsoft Office, videoconferencing platforms, and other educational technologies.
* Ability to communicate and represent ACHE professionally in academic, professional, and community settings.
* Demonstrated commitment to continuous improvement, professional development, ethical leadership, and academic integrity.
* Display professionalism for the college in all communication and interactions.
* Ability to maintain confidentiality and privacy.
* Ability to prioritize and organize numerous and varied assignments.

**ABILITIES AND COMPETENCIES ESSENTIAL TO THE FUNCTION OF THE JOB**
**Communication and Comprehension**
ACHE is in full compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and does not discriminate with regard to applicants or employees with disabilities and will make reasonable accommodations when necessary. The following are essential abilities and physical requirements for all positions at the college.
  
  

* Ability to orally communicate effectively with others with strong interpersonal skills and customer service orientation.
* Ability to work cooperatively with colleagues and supervisory staff at all levels.
* Ability to understand oral and written information, using the English language, and organize thoughts and ideas into effective forms of communication.
* Ability to make decisions which range from moderate to a significant impact on the immediate work environment, as well as outside contributors.
* Possess public communication skills that allow professional representation of ACHE to a variety of business and community customers and associates.
* Strong organizational skills.

**Problem Solving**

* Intuitively able to reason, analyze information and events, and apply judgment in order to solve problems of both a routine and complex nature.
* Expertise in negotiation.

**Physical And Sensory Abilities**

* May be exposed to short, intermittent, and/or prolonged periods of sitting and/or standing in performance of job duties.
* May be required to accomplish job duties using various types of equipment/supplies to include, but not limited to pens, pencils, calculators, computer keyboards, telephone, etc.
* May be required to transport oneself to other campus offices, conference rooms, and on occasion, to off-campus sites to attend meetings, conferences, workshops, seminars, etc.
* May require significant travel or work away from campus.
* Requires attendance at events representing ACHE both within as well as outside of the college setting.
* Frequently required to work at a desk, conference table or in meetings of various configurations.
* Frequently required to see for purposes of reading matter.
* Frequently required to hear and understand speech at normal levels.
* Occasionally required to lift items in a normal office environment.
* Ability to safely lift and carry 25 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodation.
* Frequently required to operate office and presentation equipment.

If you need assistance in the application process because of a disability, or any other reason, please contact Vicki Broadaway, Vice President of Human Resources, at 479.308.2290 or hr@achehealth.edu.
  
  
Arkansas Colleges of Health Education is an equal opportunity employer.

**Job Title**

Director of Choral Activities

**Agency**

East Texas A&M University

**Department**

Music

**Proposed Minimum Salary**

Commensurate

**Job Location**

Commerce, Texas

**Job Type**

Faculty

**Job Description**

**INSTRUCTIONS TO APPLICANT****:**

During the application process the *“My Experience*” page has a section provided “*Attachments (Resume/CV, References, Cover letter, etc.)*” to upload required documents.

* Use the Upload button to add each document.
* You will be able to upload up to 5 documents. Be aware that the maximum size allowed for any one document is 5MB.
* All documents must be electronically submitted through the Texas A&M Online Employment Services website to be considered.
* Incomplete or improperly submitted applications may be excluded from consideration.
* Please do not withdraw your application in an attempt to upload a missing document, instead please email HR for help.

**Please provide the following documents**:

* Cover Letter
* Curriculum vitae
* Selected repertoire list from the last five years
* A brief (one page) statement of teaching philosophy
* A brief (one page) statement of professional activity and goals (research and/or performance)
* Transcripts (unofficial and scanned copies are acceptable)
* The names and contact information for three professional references (at least one must be able to address teaching experience and teaching effectiveness; please indicate the teaching reference in your letter of application).
* At this time, please only upload the required documents listed above; semi-finalists may be asked to submit video recordings of their conducting in performance and rehearsal, and/or teaching.

If you need assistance, please contact us at HR.Hiring@etamu.edu

***A Presidential proclamation issued on September 19, 2025, imposes a $100,000 fee on new H-1B petitions filed after September 21, 2025. Please be advised that Texas A&M University will NOT pay this fee. Therefore, if you need immigration sponsorship for your employment, we recommend that you consult with your private immigration counsel at your own expense to ascertain whether your current immigration status would make a potential offer of employment from Texas A&M University subject to this fee.***

***In addition, on January 27, 2026, Texas Governor Abbot issued a moratorium on the filing of any new H-1B unless approved by the Texas Workforce Commission. Accordingly, if you will now or in the future require sponsorship for employment visa status this moratorium may affect our ability to employ you should you be selected as the final candidate.***

**SUMMARY:**

The School of Music at East Texas A&M University invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track **Assistant/Associate Professor in Music (Director of Choral Activities)**. The successful candidate will provide artistic, academic, and programmatic leadership for the University's choral program while contributing to teaching, Research, Scholarship, and Creative Activities (RSCA), recruitment, outreach, and service. The position includes a reduced teaching load to accommodate administrative duties, in consultation annually with the Director of the School of Music.

The School of Music serves approximately 240 music majors across instrumental, vocal, and keyboard areas and is fully accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM). It offers baccalaureate and master's degrees in music education and performance and a Bachelor of Arts in Music. The School is housed in a $30 million music building completed in 2010 containing state-of-the-art recital and concert halls, studios, rehearsal halls, classrooms, and teaching areas.

The University Chorale has an established record of significant artistic and educational achievement, including performances at Carnegie Hall, the International Music Festival of Campina Grande in Brazil, venues in France and Austria, and the 2019 Texas Music Educators Association Convention.

The Director will lead the University Chorale and Chamber Singers; teach undergraduate and graduate courses in choral conducting, choral literature, and related areas; mentor students; and contribute to the continued growth, visibility, and reputation of the choral program through high-quality performance, programming, recruitment, outreach, and professional engagement.

The position includes an administrative release; duties will be determined based on qualifications, administrative experience, demonstrated leadership skills, and School of Music needs.

**DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**Choral Program Leadership and Artistic Direction**

* Provide artistic, educational, and programmatic leadership for the University's choral program.
* Direct the University Chorale and Chamber Singers and oversee their artistic development, rehearsal, performance, and long-term growth.
* Establish high standards for ensemble musicianship, vocal technique, diction, interpretation, and performance.
* Develop an artistic vision and select repertoire representing a breadth of historical periods, styles, composers, languages, and world/cultural contexts.
* Plan concert programming and pursue appropriate performance, touring, festival, conference, and collaborative opportunities.
* Participate in strategic planning and program development for the continued growth of choral activities.

**Teaching and Student Development**

* Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in choral conducting, choral literature, and related areas as assigned.
* Provide instruction in conducting technique, score study, rehearsal methodology, choral pedagogy, repertoire, and ensemble leadership.
* Mentor and advise students pursuing careers in music education, conducting, performance, and related fields.
* Contribute to curriculum development, assessment, and program review within the choral area and School of Music.

**Music Education and Professional Preparation**

* Work with music education faculty to prepare students for careers as music educators and choral professionals.
* Supervise and mentor student teachers and maintain relationships with cooperating teachers and school administrators.
* Provide students with opportunities to develop professional skills in choral teaching and conducting.

**Recruitment, Retention, and Outreach**

* Provide leadership for recruitment and retention of undergraduate and graduate students in choral music, music education, performance, conducting, and related areas.
* Develop and implement effective recruitment initiatives and participate in auditions, clinics, workshops, festivals, prospective-student events, and other enrollment activities.
* Develop relationships with secondary-school choral directors, music educators, community organizations, and other prospective-student constituencies throughout Texas and the region.
* Represent East Texas A&M University and the School of Music at appropriate professional events and develop partnerships that strengthen the University's connections with schools, communities, and the broader choral profession.

**Collaboration and School of Music Leadership**

* Collaborate with faculty and administrators across the School of Music to support student success and program development.
* Maintain knowledge of vocal technique, vocal health, diction, repertoire, and performance preparation sufficient to address these areas within the choral program and coordinate with vocal faculty as appropriate.
* Contribute to a collegial, collaborative, and student-centered School of Music environment.

**Research, Scholarship, and Creative Activities**

* Pursue creative activity through conducting, performances, recordings, guest conducting, clinics, workshops, master classes, and related professional activities.
* Engage in scholarly activity appropriate to the candidate's expertise, including research, publication, presentation, or other professional scholarship.
* Maintain appropriate professional engagement in state, regional, national, and/or international organizations.

**Service**

* Participate in service to the School of Music, college, University, profession, and community consistent with the expectations of a tenure-track faculty appointment.
* Contribute to accreditation, assessment, strategic planning, and other institutional activities as appropriate.
* Perform other duties as assigned by the Director of the School of Music.

**MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:**

* **Education:** Doctorate in Music Education, Choral Conducting, Conducting, or a closely related field from an accredited institution; equivalent university experience and demonstrated achievement may be considered in lieu of the doctorate
* **Experience / Knowledge / Skills:**
* + Demonstrated professional experience in choral conducting and ensemble leadership.
  + Demonstrated knowledge of choral repertoire, conducting techniques, rehearsal methodology, choral pedagogy, and vocal principles relevant to choral instruction.
* **Ability to:**
* + Demonstrated ability to conduct, rehearse, and develop choral ensembles.
  + Demonstrated ability to teach and mentor students in a collegiate environment.
  + Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with faculty, staff, students, and professional colleagues.

* **Licensing/Professional** **Certifications:** N/A
* **Physical Requirements:** N/A
* **Other Requirements:** N/A

**PREFERRED EDUCATION / SKILLS/ EXPERIENCE:**

* Significant collegiate teaching and/or choral conducting experience and a record of successful collegiate ensemble leadership.
* Experience teaching choral conducting and choral literature at the undergraduate and/or graduate level.
* Demonstrated success in student recruitment, enrollment growth, or development and implementation of effective recruitment initiatives.
* Experience supervising student teachers and developing partnerships with secondary schools, community organizations, and professional music organizations.
* Demonstrated record of creative activity and/or scholarship in choral conducting, music education, vocal pedagogy, or a related field.
* Experience presenting clinics, workshops, lectures, master classes, or conducting sessions.
* Professional leadership through state, regional, national, and/or international choral or music education organizations.
* Demonstrated administrative experience involving faculty coordination, curriculum planning, recruitment, assessment, scheduling, program development, or related academic responsibilities.
* Demonstrated ability to lead collaboratively, communicate effectively, manage competing priorities, and support faculty and student success.
* Familiarity with contemporary choral pedagogy, vocal health, repertoire encompassing a breadth of historical periods and world/cultural contexts, and evidence-informed music education.
* Demonstrated knowledge of the University Interscholastic League (UIL) processes, expectations, and procedures governing Texas public school music programs, including concert and sight-reading evaluation, solo and ensemble contests, eligibility requirements, and related compliance responsibilities.
* Experience preparing students or preservice music educators for successful participation in UIL activities

**SUPERVISION OF OTHERS:**

NA

**APPLICATION REQUIREMENTS:**

* Letter of application that addresses the position qualifications
* Curriculum vitae
* Selected repertoire list from the last five years
* A brief (one page) statement of teaching philosophy
* A brief (one page) statement of professional activity and goals (research and/or performance)
* Transcripts (unofficial and scanned copies are acceptable)
* The names and contact information for three professional references (at least one must be able to address teaching experience and teaching effectiveness; please indicate the teaching reference in your letter of application).
* At this time, please only upload the required documents listed above; semi-finalists may be asked to submit video recordings of their conducting in performance and rehearsal, and/or teaching.

Review of candidates will begin on November 2nd, 2026.

All positions are security-sensitive. Applicants are subject to a criminal history investigation, and employment is contingent upon the institution’s verification of credentials and/or other information required by the institution’s procedures, including the completion of the criminal history check.

jobs.title: Open Rank Professor (T/TT) in Veterinary Medical Oncology (Cross-Posted with Open Rank NTT Professor in Veterinary Medical Oncology – Job ID: 60797)
jobs.description:
Hiring Department
  
  
Department of Veterinary Medicine & Surgery
  
  
**Job Description**
The
**College of Veterinary Medicine**
at MU is on a mission to educate and train outstanding clinicians and scientists, generate new knowledge, engage stakeholders, and foster economic growth, all of which promote and protect the health and welfare of animals and people. Our Doctor of Veterinary Medicine professional program boasts a unique curricular structure, which provides nearly two years of hands-on training in the college’s general and specialty clinics. Additionally, the College is a leader in the training of Undergraduate, Masters, and PhD students in the areas of Biomedical Sciences and Veterinary Pathobiology.
***Simply put, our mission is to Teach, Heal, Discover, and Serve.***
The
**Department of Veterinary Medicine and Surgery**
is dedicated to developing and disseminating knowledge to improve the health and well-being of animals and people through instruction, innovative research, service, and leadership. The department is home to the college’s
**Veterinary Health Center**
where our faculty provide clinical care, teach, and develop innovative treatments and therapies.
  
  
The
**Oncology Service**
in the MU College of Veterinary Medicine includes all three sub-specialties: medical, radiation, and surgical. The service is the second highest revenue generating service in our hospital, managing approximately 1,500 consultations every year. Comprised of four faculty members, the Medical Oncology team supervises six medical oncology residents annually, as well as contributes to the supervision and training of small animal rotating interns as well as oncology interns each year. In addition to patient care and treatment, house officer training, and DVM student education, the faculty in the service contribute to research activities both in the College of Veterinary Medicine, through public-private partnerships and clinical trials, and with the greater MU community through collaboration with the School of Medicine, the Ellis Fischel Cancer Center, and the NextGen Precision Medicine Initiative.
  
  
We are seeking an
**Assistant, Associate, or Full Tenure/Tenure Track Professor to join our Medical Oncology Service**
. Incumbents will be expected to maintain a strong caseload, participate in house officer training and DVM student education, as well as drive a robust translational research program that seeks to develop new and innovative treatments, improve diagnostic capabilities, increase patient outcomes, and drive understanding of cancer as a disease. They will be expected to participate in collaborative, interdisciplinary research efforts seeking to understand and treat cancer.
  
  
**Primary Responsibilities**

* Provide high-quality treatment and patient care as a member of the medical oncology service.
* Participate in the clinical and didactic teaching of veterinary students; modeling professional conduct and providing case-based instruction and feedback.
* Train, mentor, and guide house officers (both residents and interns), providing consistent instruction, feedback, coaching, and mentoring.
* Build and maintain a strong research program in an area of Veterinary Medical Oncology. The University of Missouri places a strong focus on interdisciplinary and collaborative research and values a One Health and Comparative Medine mindset and approach to research.
* Contribute to and participate in college, departmental and hospital governance and service through committee work and other activities.

This is a full-time, benefit eligible, 12-month/year appointment. Distribution of effort between teaching, research, and service will depend on the career goals of the final candidate and the needs of the department.
  
  
***This faculty opening is cross-posted with a Non-Tenure Track (Teaching / Clinical) Faculty Position in Veterinary Medical Oncology (Job ID 60797). There is one opening that may be filled at any level depending on final candidate qualifications.***
**Qualifications**
**Minimum Qualifications:**

* A Doctorate in Veterinary Medicine (DVM) or equivalent degree (such as VMD, BVSc)

Assistant Professor
  
  
**Job Summary:**
Candidates for this position will be responsible for developing and maintaining a health services or other clinical research laboratory, engaging as principal investigators and collaborators in research and obtaining/maintaining independent extramural funding. This position will work closely with researchers and clinicians in the Division of General Internal Medicine (GIM), and will have the opportunity to interact with Department of Medicine and University of Wisconsin researchers. Candidates are also provided the opportunity to grow the next generation of researchers through hands-on instruction of students, medical residents, and fellows.
  
  

* This position is full or part time, 80%-100%
* This position requires work to be completed onsite, at a designated campus work location.
* This position has been identified as a position of trust with access to vulnerable populations. The selected candidate will be required to pass an initial caregiver check to be eligible for employment under the Wisconsin Caregiver Law and every four years.
* Applicants for this position will be considered for the titles: Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, Visiting Associate Professor, Professor, or Visiting Professor. The title is determined by the experience and qualifications of the finalist.

**Key Job Responsibilities:**
The selected candidate will have protected time to develop a research program or teaching program and to engage in scholarly activities.
  
  
Conduct research in conditions treated in primary care, or delivery of primary care.
  
  
CHS and Tenure: Participate in administrative and committee work to support the clinical and scholarly missions of UW Health and the School of Medicine and Public Health. An essential part of these duties will be working in a collegial relationship with other faculty members.
  
  
All Faculty: Teach medical students, residents, and fellows.
  
  
The selected candidate will be expected to engage in active collaborative research and obtain/maintain independent extramural funding. Through these efforts, the applicant will enhance national recognition for our division
  
  
**Department:**
School of Medicine and Public Health / Department of Medicine, Division of General Internal Medicine.
  
  
The University of Wisconsin-Madison in one of the 10 largest research institutions in the country, allocating more than $1 billion annually to groundbreaking exploration. This position will be located within UW-Madison’s School of Medicine and Public Health. The Department of Medicine, the largest department in the school, empowers leaders to transform medicine. The DOM elevates everyone through meaningful mentorship, career development and opportunities to innovate. The department includes 11 divisions, and was ranked 25th in the country in extramural grant funding in FY25, with $152 million in extramural grants. We have substantial career development support for early and mid-career faculty both within the department and through collaborations across the School of Medicine and Public Health; these include programs to help develop and submit individual K awards In addition, the institution holds NIH-funded institutional career development awards through the Institute for Clinical and Translational Services (ICTR KL2 program), and the Building Interdisciplinary Research Careers in Women’s Health (BIRCH) K12 program.
  
  
At the Division of General Internal Medicine, we design and deliver state-of-the-art primary care that helps all people live their healthiest lives. We are experts in ambulatory education, population health and chronic medical care for complex patients—and we work in partnership with our world-class university and remarkable health system. Our faculty lead their own highly collaborative clinical and dissemination and implementation research laboratories (https://www.medicine.wisc.edu/general-internal-medicine/research-division-general-internal-medicine).
  
  
In addition, several members of our division are affiliated with the Center for Tobacco Research and Intervention. Federally funded for over thirty years, the center performs ground breaking tobacco research https://ctri.wisc.edu/ With Family Medicine and Pediatrics, we mentor research fellows through the HRSA funded T32 Primary Care Research Fellowship (https://www.fammed.wisc.edu/fellowships/primary-care-research/).

Negotiable, 12 month
  
  
Employees in this position can expect to receive benefits such as generous vacation, holidays, and sick leave; competitive insurances and savings accounts; retirement benefits. For more information, refer to the campus benefits webpage.
  
  

* SMPH Faculty /Academic Staff Benefits Flyer 2026
