jobs.description:
**Job Description**
Tulane University School of Medicine is seeking an accomplished physician leader to serve as
**Chief of the Division of Infectious Diseases**
within the John W. Deming Department of Medicine. The Division Chief will report to the Chair of the Department of Medicine and provide leadership across the Division’s clinical, research, and educational missions.
  
  
The Division has a strong history of excellence in infectious diseases and provides inpatient and outpatient care across multiple clinical sites, including East Jefferson General Hospital, University Medical Center New Orleans, Southeast Louisiana Veterans Health Care System, and two Ryan White-funded HIV clinics. The Division also supports an ACGME-accredited Infectious Diseases Fellowship Program and a broad research portfolio with both local and global impact.
  
  
The Division benefits from extensive opportunities for collaboration across Tulane, including the
**Tulane National Primate Research Center, Department of Microbiology and Immunology, School of Public Health and Tropical Medicine, and the Center for Translational Research in Infection and Inflammation**
. Tulane’s research infrastructure also includes advanced BSL-3 facilities supporting research in infectious diseases and emerging pathogens.
  
  
The successful candidate will build upon Tulane’s long-standing history in infectious diseases while helping guide the continued growth of the Division in clinical care, research, education, and community engagement.
  
  
**Why New Orleans?**
New Orleans offers a lifestyle and culture unlike anywhere else in the country. Known for its world-renowned cuisine, vibrant music scene, historic neighborhoods, and year-round festivals, the city provides an exceptional quality of life both professionally and personally. From award-winning restaurants and fresh Gulf seafood to Mardi Gras, Jazz Fest, and countless cultural events, New Orleans blends rich traditions with modern amenities. The city also offers a relatively affordable cost of living, easy access to outdoor recreation along the Gulf Coast, and a welcoming community that attracts people from around the world. It is an ideal place to build a fulfilling career while enjoying one of America's most unique and vibrant cities.
  
  
**Responsibilities**
Key Responsibilities:
  
  
**Education**
The Chief of the Division of Infectious Diseases will provide strategic and operational leadership across the Division's clinical, academic, research, and educational missions. Key areas of responsibility include:
  
  

* Leadership and Administration: Provide strategic direction for the Division and support faculty recruitment, development, retention, and growth.
* Clinical Excellence: Advance high-quality inpatient and outpatient infectious diseases services and support continued growth across clinical sites.
* Research and Innovation: Strengthen the Division's research portfolio and foster collaboration across Tulane University and external partners.
* Education and Training: Support excellence in medical student, resident, and fellowship education and mentorship.
* Community Engagement: Strengthen partnerships that support the health needs of New Orleans, the surrounding region, and the populations served by the Division.

The successful candidate will continue Tulane's legacy of excellence in Infectious Diseases while helping guide the Division's future growth in clinical care, research, education, and community engagement.
  
  
**Qualifications**
**QUALIFICATIONS**

* MD or DO degree.
* Board certification in Internal Medicine and Infectious Diseases.
* Eligibility for medical licensure in Louisiana.
* Minimum of 10 years of clinical experience in Infectious Diseases.
* Academic qualifications appropriate for appointment at the rank of Associate Professor or Professor at Tulane University.
* Demonstrated record of leadership, research, scholarship, and academic achievement.
* Experience mentoring and developing faculty, trainees, and other healthcare professionals.
* Strong interpersonal and collaborative leadership skills with the ability to work effectively across clinical and academic environments.

**About Us**
Tulane University is an equal opportunity educator and employer committed to providing an education and employment environment free of unlawful discrimination, harassment, and retaliation. Legally protected demographic classifications (such as a person’s race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, shared ancestry, disability, genetics, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws) are not relied upon as an eligibility, selection or participation criteria for Tulane’s employment or educational programs or activities.
  
  
Tulane University is responsible for providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities throughout the applicant screening process. If you need assistance in completing an application or during any phase of the interview process, please contact the Office of Human Resources by phone at 504-865-4748 or by email at hr@tulane.edu .

This full-time faculty position is on-campus and in-person.
  
  
The Harris College of Nursing and Health Sciences at Texas Christian University seeks candidates for a 9-month tenure-track position in nursing as the W.F. “Tex” & Polly Rankin Endowed Professor in Nursing. Minimum requirements include an earned PhD in nursing or a related field, demonstrated effective teaching in higher education for at least three years, and an established record of funded research and scholarly work.
  
  
Candidates must meet criteria for appointment as an Associate or Full Professor. Applicants for this position will have designated resources to support their research program and travel. Educational preparation and clinical expertise in adult medical-surgical, critical care nursing preferred. The position(s) is on-campus and in-person. Candidates must hold or be eligible to obtain a current, valid, unencumbered license to practice as a Registered Nurse in the state of Texas. Salary is commensurate with education and experience.
  
  
**Department Details**
TCU Nursing is renowned for its commitment to academic excellence, clinical proficiency, and compassionate patient care. Located in Fort Worth, Texas, TCU Nursing offers a comprehensive range of undergraduate and graduate nursing programs designed to prepare students for diverse roles in healthcare.
  
  
Our programs build on and reinforce a broad foundation of liberal studies. At the undergraduate level, the Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) program blends rigorous classroom instruction with hands-on clinical experiences. Students receive a solid foundation in nursing theory, evidence-based practice, and patient-centered care. Our graduate and doctoral programs are fully online and prepare registered nurses for leadership and/or advanced practice in a variety of settings.
  
  
TCU's nursing faculty are distinguished by their expertise, dedication to teaching, and active involvement in research that advances the field of nursing. Our faculty includes accomplished educators, researchers, and practitioners who have an intentional desire to advance health and the field of nursing education and practice.
  
  
Our simulation and practice labs are equipped with state-of-the-art technology to prepare students across levels for patient care before entering the hospital setting. Students assume considerable responsibility for their own learning and are expected to become increasingly independent and competent in the exercise of clinical judgment, clinical reasoning, and the application of the nursing process to a variety of problems and situations.
  
  
As a result of strong partnerships with regional health care systems, our clinical placements allow students to apply their knowledge under the guidance of experienced faculty and healthcare professionals. We emphasize the importance of interprofessional collaboration and global engagement, preparing students to work effectively within healthcare teams and make meaningful contributions to the health and well-being of individuals and communities across a variety of settings.
  
  
**School/College Description**
The Harris College of Nursing & Health Sciences consists of programs that prepare future health care and human services professionals. The academic units within Harris College – Applied Health Sciences, Communication Sciences & Disorders, Occupational Therapy, Kinesiology, Nurse Anesthesia, Nursing, and Social Work – are home to 1,900 students who are supported by committed and talented faculty and staff. Harris College supports the mission, vision, and values of TCU; we prepare global citizens to think and practice as ethical leaders in health care and educational settings.
  
  
Harris College offers 20 degree pathways in our health-related disciplines. Students benefit from learning experiences in campus laboratories and hospitals, clinics, schools, fitness facilities, and community service agencies throughout the Dallas-Fort Worth Area. On campus, the Miller Speech & Hearing Clinic provides services for more than 300 families each year and serves as a professional practice site for students majoring in speech pathology and habilitation of the deaf. TCU Nursing and the School of Nurse Anesthesia provide innovative learning experiences in their state-of-the-art simulation centers.
  
  
The faculty and students at Harris College actively engage in research for the purpose of improving health and well-being. Undergraduate and graduate students have opportunities to form mentoring relationships with internationally recognized faculty as they conduct studies in such areas as pharmacogenetics, carbohydrate metabolism, exercise physiology, health disparities, heart disease, aging, Parkinson’s disease, caregiving, language development in children with hearing loss, and forgiveness among others. Our graduates are competent, compassionate, and in demand in the workforce.
  
  
**About TCU**
University & Fort Worth Description:
  
  
Founded in 1873, Texas Christian University is a world-class, private, Carnegie-classified national research university located in Fort Worth, Texas. Inspired by its mission and core values of integrity, engagement, community, and excellence, TCU consistently ranks among the top universities and colleges in the United States.
  
  
TCU’s campus — regularly ranked among the nation’s most beautiful — spans 302 acres in a primarily residential area just minutes from downtown.
  
  
The university comprises nine schools and colleges offering 117 areas of undergraduate study, 62 master’s level programs, and 37 areas of doctoral study. TCU is a leader across several disciplines, including health care, business, energy, and the arts. Total enrollment stands at 12,980, including 11,152 undergraduates and 1,828 graduate students. Students are supported by over 2,200 faculty and staff, including more than 700 full-time faculty members.
  
  
**About Fort Worth**
Fort Worth blends the approachable charm of a smaller city with the amenities, cultural energy, and distinctive personality of a major metro. As the nation’s 11th-largest city, with a rapidly growing population of more than 1 million, Fort Worth and TCU share a relationship that spans more than a century — one that continues to deepen as many Horned Frogs choose to stay after graduation, drawn by the region’s thriving job market. Part of the Dallas-Fort Worth metropolitan area — the nation’s fourth-largest and a top tourism destination — Fort Worth earned recognition from U.S. News & World Report in 2025 as the No. 4 best big city to live in the United States.
  
  
Fort Worth offers an impressive array of cultural, educational, and entertainment opportunities, anchored by three world-class art museums — the Kimbell Art Museum, the Modern Art Museum of Fort Worth, and the Amon Carter Museum of American Art. The Bass Performance Hall stands as one of the premier performance venues in the country. Throughout the year, residents and visitors alike enjoy concerts, film festivals, and other cultural events at Sundance Square, Dickies Arena, Panther Island, and Near Southside venues.
  
  
**Required Application Materials & Application Instructions**
Applications should be submitted online through the TCU Human Resources website at jobs.tcu.edu. You may search for this position by entering the 6-digit requisition number located above or by entering the title in the search field.
  
  
Please provide a (1) letter of interest, (2) curriculum vita, (3) teaching philosophy,
  
  

* planned program of research including external funding experience/plan, and
* names and contact information for three professional references.

Letters of recommendation will be requested at a later time in the process from your three references. Your references will receive an email from TCU asking them to upload their LOR on your behalf.
  
  
**Employment Values Statement**
Texas Christian University values Integrity, Engagement, Community, and Excellence in the workplace. TCU treats applicants and employees with fairness and respect. TCU hires and promotes individuals based on their qualifications and their commitment to making a positive impact on our student-centered community. TCU is an equal opportunity employer and follows all applicable employment laws. TCU fairly considers all qualified individuals, ensuring we are a workplace free from unlawful discrimination and harassment.

Assistant Professor of Studio Art (Printmaking)

$56,000 - $62,000

School of Art

08/15/2027

**About this opportunity:**

The School of Art at Ball State University welcomes applications for a full-time, tenure-line Assistant Professor of Studio Art with a specialty in printmaking. The ideal candidate will be a creative teacher, thoughtful mentor, and collaborative colleague who will foster interdisciplinary collaboration across the School of Art's many studio areas.
  
  
The School of Art has over forty full-time faculty and staff and offers state-of-the-art facilities serving approximately 700 undergraduate majors. Programs at the BA, BS, and BFA levels include art education, art history, graphic design, graphic design studies, animation production, illustration, game art/design, visual effects, and a studio art program that includes drawing, painting, printmaking, ceramics, glass, metals + jewelry, sculpture, photography, and video and new media. Glick Center for Glass. Students and faculty work closely with David Owsley Museum of Art on campus, among the finest university art collections in the nation. jobs.title: Assistant Professor, Psychology (Tenure Track)
jobs.description:
The Department of Psychology at Elmhurst University invites applications for a tenure-track, assistant professor position with an emphasis in Cognitive Neuroscience, broadly defined, beginning August 2027. The successful candidate will have demonstrated potential for excellence in undergraduate teaching and mentoring, and outstanding potential as a professor in a comprehensive liberal arts setting. The candidate will need to teach upper-level courses related to their area of expertise (including Cognitive Neuroscience), as well as lower-level methodology courses (such as Research Methods in Psychology), and other courses depending on candidate ability and department need as part of a 3/3 load. Preference will be given to candidates who can adapt their research program to a small, liberal arts environment and involve undergraduate students in their research. In addition, faculty are expected to contribute to the Department and University through service activities and advising.

The Department of Psychology serves hundreds of majors and minors, participates in the university’s core curriculum, and supports other programs of study including the nursing program and the new neuroscience major. Candidate materials should demonstrate their commitment to creating an inclusive learning environment for a diverse student body.

Applicants must have a Ph.D. in psychology (or a related field, e.g., neuroscience); however, ABD with significant progress towards the degree and a completion date prior to August 2027 will also be considered. ABD candidates should address this concern in their materials. Interested candidates must apply online by clicking the "Apply for this job" button below. Please submit a letter of interest, curriculum vitae, three references, statement of teaching philosophy, statement of research interests, diversity statement, evidence of teaching effectiveness (such as a course syllabus), graduate transcripts, and any other relevant supporting documents through the online application system. If there are any questions, please send all inquiries by email to Patrick Nebl, Ph.D., Search Committee Chairperson, at patrick.nebl@elmhurst.edu.

For full consideration, materials must be submitted by November 1.

**Position Status:** Exempt

**Salary Range:** $65,000 - $72,000. This is the expected salary range for this position. The actual salary offered will depend on a candidate's experience and education, and departmental budget.

Responsibilities

Responsibilities for this position include course preparation, teaching, grading, and being available to students who have questions or require assistance; establishing a research program that actively includes undergraduate students; and service to the department and University.

**Other Responsibilities**

* Demonstrates a strong commitment to continuous improvement.
* Supports the mission, vision, and values of Elmhurst University.
* Performs other faculty-related duties consistent with the department and University's mission and needs as assigned.

  
**Requirements**

**Minimum Qualifications**

Applicants must have a Ph.D. (ABD with significant progress towards the degree and a completion date prior to August 2027 will also be considered) in a psychological discipline, demonstrated potential for excellence in undergraduate teaching and mentoring, and outstanding potential as a professor in a comprehensive liberal arts setting.

**Preferred Qualifications**

Applicant specialty should allow for the development of a successful research program at a primarily undergraduate institution that incorporates undergraduate students.

**Working Conditions/Physical Requirements**

The essential functions of this position are primarily performed in an indoor setting with limited exposure to outdoor weather conditions. Work is often sedentary in nature and requires remaining in a stationary position for extended periods. Required abilities include speaking and hearing for in-person and virtual communication, using close and distance vision when reading documents or viewing screens, and performing tasks with repetitive fine motor skills. Work may require occasional lifting, bending, carrying, or otherwise moving objects weighing up to 15 pounds. Qualified applicants who can perform the essential functions of this position with or without reasonable accommodations will be considered.

 **Benefits**

An overview of Elmhurst University benefits is available **here****.**

**Additional Instructions for Applicants**

Interested candidates should electronically submit a 1) cover letter, 2) curriculum vitae, 3) detailed list of three references, 4) statement of teaching philosophy, 5) statement of research interests and plans, 6) diversity statement, 7) evidence of teaching effectiveness, and 8) graduate transcripts.

Applicants who proceed in the process will be asked to submit three letters of recommendation.

If you have any questions, please contact Dr. Patrick Nebl in the Department of Psychology at patrick.nebl@elmhurst.edu. Review of credentials will begin November 1, 2026.

jobs.title: Asst Prof of Practice, NTT - Crim & Crim Just
jobs.description:
PCN 1096

**Position Overview:**

The Department of Criminology and Criminal Justice at Merrimack College is seeking a full-time Assistant Professor of Practice, Non-Tenure-Track (NTT) faculty member to join the department starting in Fall 2027.

This 9- month faculty position offers an opportunity to play an important role in a growing and evolving department. The Department of Criminology and Criminal Justice offers undergraduate and graduate programs designed to prepare students to understand complex issues of crime, justice, public service, and community safety from multiple perspectives. Our programs include the Bachelor of Arts in Criminology and Criminal Justice; the Bachelor of Science in Forensic Science, offered jointly with the Department of Biochemistry; the Master of Science in Criminology and Criminal Justice; the Master of Public Administration; and a new 96-credit degree pathway in Criminal Justice.

We seek candidates who connect academic learning with professional practice, bringing industry insights and networks from law enforcement agencies, courts, corrections, victim services, nonprofit and community organizations, government agencies, or other organizations working across the broader criminal justice ecosystem to create applied learning opportunities and mentor students toward successful careers.

**Primary Responsibilities**

* Teach required undergraduate and graduate courses in Research Methods and Statistics in Criminology and Criminal Justice and related areas;
* Serve as a mentor to students exploring career pathways, internships, applied experiences, and graduate study;
* Develop partnerships with criminal justice and related organizations;
* Represent the Department of Criminology and Criminal Justice at Admissions events.

**Required Qualifications**

* Doctoral degree in Criminology Criminal Justice Law Public Administration or a related field.;
* Relevant professional or research experience in criminal justice law public safety victim services law enforcement courts corrections government nonprofit or community-based organizations or another field related to the department’s programs;
* Demonstrated ability or potential to be an effective and engaging college level teacher who can connect academic concepts with contemporary issues and professional practice;
* Preparation to teach courses in research methods and/or statistics in criminology and criminal justice as well as courses related to the candidate’s areas of expertise;
* Interest and ability to build relationships with professionals agencies and community organizations that can enhance students’ classroom experiential learning and career opportunities;
* Ability to work collaboratively with faculty and staff and contribute to the department’s undergraduate and graduate programs.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience teaching or supporting student learning at the undergraduate or graduate level.
* Expertise in domestic violence and/or victimology although candidates with expertise in other areas of criminology and criminal justice are encouraged to apply.
* Experience mentoring students, interns or early-career professionals.
* Experience with internships field-based learning community-engaged projects or other forms of experiential education.
* Professional relationships within the criminal justice or public service community that could contribute to student learning and career exploration

**Application Materials Should Include:**

* Resume or CV
* Cover letter stating motivation and interest in the position, citing experience relevant to the qualifications and including experience with, and commitment to, our Catholic Augustinian mission and our values.
* Teaching Statement
* Contact information for three professional references

We will review applications immediately and continue reviewing until the positions are filled.

**Compensation**

The expected 9-month base salary range (paid over 12 months) for the Assistant Professor of Practice position is $ 78 000-$ 90 000. The actual pay offered to the selected candidate will be determined based on factors such as but not limited to candidate qualifications and prior experience scope of responsibilities internal equity and market considerations

**Work Location**

This is an on-campus position as employees are essential in order to provide a fully on-campus, residential college experience for our students and the community.

This position is subject to the successful completion of a criminal background check.

**Statement on Our Mission**

Merrimack College is a Catholic Augustinian institution of higher education committed to building an accepting and respectful community. Our mission is to enlighten minds, engage hearts and empower lives and is inspired by our Catholic faith and the Augustinian tradition of seeking truth through inquiry and dialogue.

Merrimack College seeks candidates who understand, respect, and can contribute to Merrimack’s Catholic and Augustinian mission. All candidates should describe in their application how they will foster a culture that supports our mission.

**About Merrimack College**

The only Catholic, Augustinian institution of higher education in New England, Merrimack College is a private, independent, coeducational institution with more than 4,100 undergraduate, 2,500 graduate students and 50 doctoral students from 48 states and 63 countries. The College features more than 160 career-focused undergraduate, professional and graduate programs, all taught by exceptional faculty who are passionate about their subject and student success. The College has six schools: arts and sciences, engineering and computational sciences, nursing and health sciences, education and social policy, the Girard school of business and the graduate school of counseling and social work. The College’s suburban 220-acre campus is just north of Boston in North Andover, Massachusetts. Merrimack is a Master’s Colleges and Universities/Larger Programs (M1) institution in the Carnegie Classification of Institutions of Higher Education. Merrimack is one of the fastest growing educational institutions in the country and has steadily climbed up in the U.S. News & World Report’s ranking of Best Colleges, ranking 38th in the Regional Universities North category in 2026. Merrimack is a NCAA Division I athletic institution.

Merrimack College is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

jobs.title: Professor of Endodontics - Full-Time
jobs.company: University of Pittsburgh School of Dental Medicine
jobs.description:
The University of Pittsburgh School of Dental Medicine invites applications for the position of Chair of the Department of Endodontics. This is an open-rank, full-time appointment stream (nontenure) faculty position. The academic rank will be determined as commensurate with the candidate's qualifications and experience.
  
  
The Chair will have a unique opportunity to lead a vibrant, nationally recognized department with a longstanding tradition of excellence in education, clinical care, research, and service. Supported by a thriving clinical enterprise, the department is well positioned for continued growth and innovation. The successful candidate will build on these strengths to shape the department's future, expand its impact, and foster excellence across its academic, clinical, and research missions. A key expectation of the role is to recruit, develop, and retain outstanding faculty while attracting highly talented residents who will contribute to the department's continued national prominence. Working collaboratively with faculty, staff, students, residents, and institutional leaders, the Chair will advance initiatives that promote oral health equity, strengthen community-based education, expand access to care in rural and underserved communities, enhance translational and population health research, and further elevate evidence-based clinical practice.
  
  
Key responsibilities include: provide visionary leadership aligned with the school's mission to improve oral and overall health through education, research, and service; didactic and clinical instruction of residents, scholarly activities, and service; provide support to the program director of the Advanced Dental Education and Residency Program in Endodontics; engage in scholarship; mentor faculty in teaching and in securing extramural research funding; advance curricular integration of endodontics in predoctoral and residency programs; and manage departmental resources, personnel, and strategic planning with transparency and fiscal accountability. Additional departmental administrative duties may also apply. Participation in the University Dental Health Services faculty practice is also available.
  
  
Qualified applicants must hold a dental degree and an advanced education certificate in Endodontics from a CODA-accredited program. The applicant must be a Diplomate of the American Board of Endodontics (ABE) and be able to obtain and maintain a Pennsylvania dental license. The applicant should have a minimum of five years of clinical practice and a minimum of five years of teaching experience as a full-time or part-time faculty member associated with an endodontic department. Preference will be given to those with additional academic and/or leadership training, a documented record of achievement in teaching, scholarship, and service related to the specialty of endodontics; and demonstrated leadership experience and success in fostering collaborative, interdisciplinary teams.
  
  
The University of Pittsburgh is a top-ranked public research institution and is currently ranked 7th among U.S. universities in NIH funding. The School of Dental Medicine is ranked 7th in FY25 in NIDCR funding among U.S. dental schools. The school is located on the University's main campus in Pittsburgh, contiguous with the other five health science schools. UPMC is an internationally renowned academic medical center and health care enterprise with a robust infrastructure to support clinicians with innovative clinical programs and biomedical and health sciences research, making discoveries that save lives and change the landscape of patient care. As part of the clinical practice and faculty of the University of Pittsburgh, the practitioner will have the opportunity to collaborate with clinicians, innovators, and investigators from around the world and become part of a vibrant community of health care providers dedicated to making a difference in their chosen field and in the lives of others.
  
  
To apply, please go to join.pitt.edu, select Faculty Positions, and search for keyword 26004728. Please upload a curriculum vitae, the names and contact information for three references, and a cover letter that describes your interest in the position, qualifications, and experience; outlines your vision for the future of the department; and explains why you want to join the Pitt Dental Medicine team. The search committee will begin reviewing applications upon receipt. Only applicants who appear best qualified will be invited to a personal interview.
  
  
Dent Med-Endodontics
  
  
**Assignment Category**
Full-time regular
  
  
**Bargaining Unit Eligibility**
This position may be bargaining unit eligible
  
  
**Child Protection Clearances**
The following PA Act 153 clearances and background checks are required prior to commencement of employment and as a condition of continued employment: PA State Police Criminal Record Check, FBI Criminal Record Check, PA Child Abuse History Clearance.
  
  
**Required Attachments**
Cover Letter, Curriculum Vitae, Letters of Recommendation, Teaching Statement, Teaching Evaluations

jobs.title: Open Rank Academic Position – Emergency Medicine Physician: Assistant Professor, Associate Professor or Professor
jobs.description:
**Job Summary**
The Department of Emergency Medicine at the University of Colorado School of ‎Medicine is currently recruiting Emergency Medicine Physicians to serve as ‎academic faculty with expertise in: educating learners (students, residents, and ‎fellows), conducting high impact research, and disseminating scholarly activity. The ‎successful candidate may practice clinical subspecialty medicine in one of the ‎following areas: administration and operations, education, wilderness medicine, point ‎of care ultrasound, sports medicine, palliative care, climate change, toxicology, ‎critical care, quality and patient safety or another approved subspecialty. This role ‎includes patient care and bedside teaching, as well as didactic teaching of ‎emergency medicine residents and medical students.‎
  
  
The Emergency Department at the University of Colorado Hospital is a 55,000 ‎square foot state of the art facility with 76 treatment areas including a 16-bed ‎observation unit and is a major teaching site for the Denver Health Residency in ‎Emergency Medicine. The University of Colorado Hospital is a 600+ bed quaternary ‎care referral center, level I trauma center, ABA verified burn center, joint commission ‎certified comprehensive stroke center of excellence and is the academic flagship of ‎the University of Colorado Health System. Current ED patient volumes are in excess ‎of 100,000 visits per year with anticipated growth of 1-2% annually.‎
  
  
**Job Responsibilities include but are not limited to:‎**
**Clinical Responsibilities:‎**

* Possess a strong dedication to clinical activities, both broadly in emergency ‎medicine and as they relate to an individual’s areas of expertise and ‎experience, including providing care to adult and pediatric patients.‎
* Participate in clinical activity that will result in promotion as stipulated in ‎the CU School of Medicine Faculty Handbook.‎
* Serve as an attending in the emergency department at one of the approved ‎sites, including: any affiliated free-standing emergency department, virtual ‎health care, Broomfield Hospital, Highlands Ranch Hospital, or the University ‎of Colorado Hospital.‎
* Participate in the rotating sick call coverage schedule per departmental or ‎practice site guidelines, if applicable.‎
* Complete necessary CME per departmental and/or practice site guidelines.‎
* Serve as a committee member as needed by the Department or practice site ‎on an ad hoc basis.‎

**Teaching Responsibilities:‎**

* Dispense excellent bedside teaching and supervision. ‎
* Participate in didactic education for emergency medicine residents and ‎students.‎

**Scholarly Activities:‎**

* Be academically productive publishing at least two peer-reviewed ‎manuscripts or equivalent products of scholarship per year

**Research Activities (applicable for Research Faculty applicants only):‎**

* Submit applications for federal funding with the goal of anticipated funding ‎within the first 2-3 years of hire‎. Publish at least 3 peer-reviewed original research manuscripts per year, ‎understanding that publication cycles are variable and there is a ramp up ‎period.‎

**Administrative Activities:‎**

* Participate in improving patient safety, clinical quality or patient experience.‎
* Participate in ad hoc and established Department of Emergency Medicine, ‎University of Colorado Hospital, or School of Medicine committees as ‎needed.‎

**Work Location:**

* Onsite – this role is expected to work onsite and is located in Denver, CO ‎metropolitan area.‎ The Department of Emergency Medicine at the University of Colorado School of ‎Medicine is dedicated to delivering superlative patient care, providing an ‎environment where training and education thrive and innovation and discovery are ‎fostered.‎

**Why Join Us**
The Department of Emergency Medicine is based at the Anschutz Medical Campus ‎in Aurora Colorado. jobs.title: Tenure-Track Assistant or Tenured Associate Professor Faculty Position in Artificial Intelligence and Industrial Experiments
jobs.description:
**Indiana University Bloomington** (IUB) invites applications for one **tenure-track assistant or associate professor** in the **Luddy School of Informatics, Computing, and Engineering** in the field of **AI and Industrial Experiments.** We seek candidates to join IU’s outstanding **Computing and Engineering** research program to lead research in areas such as machine learning, agentic AI, edge AI, physical AI and AI safety.

We encourage applications from scholars who apply interdisciplinary perspectives and share important research overlap with current IUB scholars while also offering new dimensions that will expand and strengthen the Luddy School’s research program.

These 10‐month appointments would ideally start **August 1, 2027**, although an earlier or later start date is negotiable. Applications received by November 1, 2026, will receive full consideration, and applications will be accepted until the positions are filled.

**Responsibilities:** Tenured/tenure-track faculty at Indiana University Bloomington are expected to substantially contribute to the overall academic excellence of their department by developing and/or maintaining a robust research portfolio including pursuing and obtaining major extramural research funding to conduct cutting-edge research both as a corresponding principal investigator and a collaborating investigator; teaching and mentoring undergraduate and/or graduate students as designated by the department chairperson; and actively providing service within the department, school and university alongside active engagement with the profession and/or the community. We invite applications from candidates whose research advances the foundations and frontiers of artificial intelligence and its translation into industrial practice. Candidates with special interest in the following areas are encouraged to apply:

* machine learning methods underpinning foundation models;
* agentic AI and AI-based model orchestration;
* edge AI and resource-constrained deployment;
* physical and embodied AI, including industrial control, and cyber-physical systems; and trustworthy AI, covering safety, robustness, privacy, and alignment.
  

We welcome work that spans theory, methodology, and real-world experimentation, particularly research validated through industrial-scale systems, datasets, or testbeds. Candidates with experience in industry, or with a demonstrated record of collaboration with industrial partners on applied AI problems, are especially encouraged to apply, as are those whose work bridges academic inquiry with the operational demands of deployed AI systems.

These positions are located on the campus of Indiana University, Bloomington (IUB) in Bloomington, Indiana, and successful candidates are expected to work on the IUB campus to allow full engagement with the department, school, campus, and community. Indiana University bases its tenure and promotion recommendations upon performance in three areas including research, teaching, and service. All individuals hired through this initiative are expected to excel in research and provide strong performance in teaching and service.

**Minimum Qualifications:** Applicants should possess a PhD in **computer science, engineering, data science, or AI** (or a related field) and be committed to excellence in scholarship and teaching at the undergraduate and graduate level.

Candidates considered for appointment with tenure must demonstrate a record of scholarly achievement appropriate to such an appointment, including extramurally funded research as a corresponding principal investigator, current funding or strong potential to secure external funding, established record of publications and scholarly work, and experience leading sizeable research initiatives.

**Application Procedures:** Review of applications will begin **November 1, 2026** and continue until all positions are filled. Application materials should include:

* Cover letter (maximum of 3 pages in length, identifying your application for a position with tenure (associate professor) or a tenure-track position (assistant professor), summarizing your qualifications, and interest in the position.
* Current Curriculum Vitae
* Research Statement (maximum of 4 pages in length)
* Teaching Statement (maximum of 2 pages in length) OPTIONAL
* Up to three representative scholarly publications (optional) OPTIONAL
* Contact information for three professional references
  + Professional references for **applicants for tenure-track positions** will only be solicited for those selected for a screening interviews.
  + Professional references for **applicants for positions with tenure** will only be solicited for those selected for a finalist interview and/or job offer.

Applicants for associate professor should apply at: **https://indiana.peopleadmin.com/postings/34483**

All queries about the position or the application procedures should be addressed to Dr. Haixu Tang, search chairperson, at hatang@iu.edu or Dr. Cindy Broderick, search coordinator, at **faculty1@iu.edu**.

Before a conditional offer of employment with tenure is finalized, candidates will be asked to disclose any pending investigations or previous findings of sexual or professional misconduct. They will also be required to authorize an inquiry by Indiana University Bloomington with all current and former employers along these lines. The relevance of information disclosed or ascertained in the context of this process to a candidate’s eligibility for hire will be evaluated by Indiana University Bloomington on a case-by-case basis. Applicants should be aware, however, that Indiana University Bloomington takes the matters of sexual and professional misconduct very seriously.

  

*Indiana University is an equal opportunity employer and provider of* *ADA* *services and prohibits discrimination in hiring.* ***See Indiana University Notice of Non-Discrimination here which includes contact information.***

**About Indiana University Bloomington**: Founded in 1820, Indiana University-Bloomington (IUB) is the flagship campus of Indiana University. Located in Bloomington, IN., IUB constantly strives to embody its mission to create, disseminate, preserve, and apply knowledge. It does so through its commitments to cutting-edge research, scholarship, arts, and creative activity; inspired and challenging undergraduate, graduate, professional, and lifelong educational programs; meaningful experiences outside the classroom; expansive global educational opportunities; first-rate library and museum collections; and far-reaching economic development and impact in the state and region.

IUB is a member of the prestigious Association of American Universities (AAU) since 1909, is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission and is a member of the North Central Association. With over 47,000 undergraduate and graduate students, the campus has 16 degree-granting colleges and schools offering 300+ undergraduate majors, 300+ Master’s degrees, and 150+ doctoral and professional degree opportunities. Known for its Indiana limestone facades and green spaces throughout, IUB is widely considered one of the country’s most beautiful college campuses.

The **Luddy School of Informatics, Computing, and Engineering at Indiana University Bloomington** is a nationally recognized leader in computing, artificial intelligence, data science, information technology, and engineering education and research. As one of the largest and most comprehensive schools of its kind in the United States, Luddy brings together distinguished faculty, innovative researchers, and talented students in a collaborative environment dedicated to advancing discovery and addressing complex societal challenges through data-driven and computational approaches.
  
  
The School’s interdisciplinary **Data Science Program** prepares students to excel in a rapidly evolving landscape shaped by artificial intelligence and advanced analytics through rigorous training in statistics, machine learning, AI, data management, and data visualization. Supported by a vibrant research ecosystem that spans AI, intelligent systems, health informatics, cybersecurity, and computational science, the program equips graduates with the technical expertise, ethical foundation, and collaborative skills needed to transform complex data into actionable insights and innovative solutions across academia, industry, government, and the nonprofit sector.

  

**Basic Qualifications**

**Minimum Qualifications:** Applicants should possess a PhD in **computer science, engineering, data science, or AI** (or a related field) and be committed to excellence in scholarship and teaching at the undergraduate and graduate level.

Candidates considered for appointment with tenure must demonstrate a record of scholarly achievement appropriate to such an appointment, including extramurally funded research as a corresponding principal investigator, current funding or strong potential to secure external funding, established record of publications and scholarly work, and experience leading sizeable research initiatives.

  

**Department Contact for Questions**

All queries about the position or the application procedures should be addressed to Dr. Haixu Tang, search chairperson, at hatang@iu.edu or Dr. Cindy Broderick, search coordinator, at **faculty1@iu.edu**.

The College of Nursing and Health Sciences (CONHS) at Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi (TAMUCC) invites applications for a tenure-track Associate Professor of Nursing Practice beginning Fall 2027. This is a 9-month academic appointment with a possible summer appointment and will be located at the Corpus Christi campus. Faculty members are required to be physically on campus as needed to contribute to academic mission of the College and University.
  
  
****Job Description****
All tenure and tenure-track positions will have responsibilities in research, teaching, and service missions. Tenured/tenure-track faculty are expected to teach students, pursue a robust program of research, seek external funding, and disseminate research findings. Faculty are expected to model exemplar professional behavior through work with students, peers, administration, and community colleagues and to provide student support to include mentoring, advising, recruiting, and DNP student project supervision. Teaching responsibilities ensures adherence to program policies, course objectives, program outcomes and current teaching, clinical, and simulation best practices and safety measures. All faculty are expected to maintain content and clinical mastery, and to participate in college, university and professional service activities. Active participation in college and university committees and activities is required. The faculty members will maintain an active program of scholarship and disseminate scholarly work through peer-reviewed publications, presentations, and other appropriate venues.
  
  
Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi is a vibrant, Hispanic and Minority Serving R2 Doctoral Research Institution that proudly provides a solid academic reputation, renowned faculty, and highly rated degree programs since 1947. The University has a heritage of teaching excellence with innovation in research and community engagement as part of the distinguished Texas A&M System. TAMU-CC is the only university in the nation located on its own island, at the heart of the Texas Gulf Coast. With palm tree lined pathways throughout the campus, nearby natural wetlands, a scenic hike-and-bike trail and pristine views of the beach and bays, Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi is a first-choice institution.
  
  
****Required Qualifications:****

* Candidates must hold a research focused PhD in Nursing from an accredited institution.
* Current unencumbered RN and/or APRN License in the State of Texas by the time of appointment.
* An established program of research and scholarship with a record of successful funding.
* Experience in higher education including classroom and/or clinical teaching.
* To be considered for an Associate Professor rank, a minimum of five (5) years of experience at the Assistant Professor or comparable rank is required.

****Preferred Qualifications****

* Post‐ doctoral education/training.
* Experience coordinating academic nursing programs
* Experience in teaching and developing nursing leadership and management courses.
* Records of professional service at local or national levels.
* Teaching experience at the graduate level
* Experience with web-based course delivery, including on-line course development, online teaching, and application of best practices in online education
* Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively across disciplines and with community practice partners.

**TO APPLY: http://hr.tamucc.edu/careers/**
**All required documentation must be uploaded to be considered for the position.**
**A Completed Application Will Include:**

* A letter of application addressing qualifications listed and a teaching and research philosophy statement.
* A current curriculum vitae.
* Three (3) professional references including name, address, title, telephone number, and email addresses- including a previous or current supervisor.
* Copies of unofficial transcripts for undergraduate and graduate coursework.

The job posting will remain open until a finalist is selected. Applications will be reviewed immediately.
  
  
***NOTE:
*Employment may be impacted by the Presidential proclamation issued on September 19, 2025 and the moratorium issued by Texas Governor Abbott on January 27, 2026.****

Our faculty, students, residents, and fellows have had their research published in top-tier peer-reviewed journals. With a group practice, UNLV Health provides care to more than 10,000 patients per month in its 17 primary care and specialty care clinics, and its partner hospitals.

from an accredited college or university as recognized by the United States Department of Education and/or the Council on Higher Education Accreditation (CHEA). jobs.title: Assistant Professor - AI for Biology - Electrical Engineering & Computer Sciences and Center for Computational Biology
jobs.description:
**Position overview Position title:** Assistant Professor Salary range: The current salary range for the Assistant Professor position is $111,400-$163,200 (9-month academic year salary); however, off-scale salary and other components of pay, which would yield compensation that is higher than this range, are offered to meet competitive conditions. Anticipated start: July 1, 2027 Application Window
  
**Open date:** September 25, 2026
  
**Next review date:** Monday, Nov 9, 2026 at 11:59pm (Pacific Time)
  
Apply by this date to ensure full consideration by the committee.
  
**Final date:** Monday, Nov 9, 2026 at 11:59pm (Pacific Time)
  
Applications will continue to be accepted until this date. Position description
  
The Department of Electrical Engineering & Computer Sciences (EECS) and the Center for Computational Biology (CCB) at UC Berkeley invite applications for one approved tenure-track position at the Assistant Professor level in the area of artificial intelligence (AI) for biology. Memberships in related institutes and initiatives or affiliations with other UC Berkeley departments or schools may also be considered. The EECS Department and the Center for Computational Biology have several related faculty positions open or opening soon. Please visit our EECS Faculty Positions website and the CCB Careers website to view these listings. If you are qualified for and wish to be considered for more than one position, please submit a separate application for each.
  
**About the Department :** The EECS department is part of the College of Engineering (COE) and the College of Computing, Data Science, and Society (CDSS). It offers one of the strongest research and instructional programs in this field anywhere in the world. The department's key strength is its array of cross-disciplinary, team-driven projects. The integration of EE and CS forms the core, with strong interactions that extend into many other disciplines.
  
**About the Center :** CCB is an academic unit under the College of Computing, Data Science, and Society (CDSS). It offers a PhD degree program, as well as interdisciplinary collaboration and research for diverse areas across computational biology. The center features distinguished faculty and graduate students from more than a dozen academic departments across six colleges at UC Berkeley.
  
**About the Position :** EECS and CCB are seeking applicants developing innovative AI and machine learning (ML) methods that significantly advance our understanding of complex biological systems and address high-impact problems in biology. Relevant research areas include, but are not limited to the following: AI/ML for predicting cellular phenotypes and responses to genetic, molecular, and environmental perturbations; modeling of molecular interactions, including interactions among proteins, nucleic acids, and small molecules; genotype-to-phenotype prediction across molecular, cellular, and organismal scales; AI/ML for genome and biomolecule engineering; and method development for computational genomics, including the integration of large-scale single-cell, spatial, imaging, and multimodal biological data. Across these areas, we are particularly interested in candidates who develop novel and broadly applicable AI/ML methodology for learning from complex biological data, with the potential to uncover fundamental biological principles and enable new approaches to understanding, predicting, and manipulating biological systems.
  
UC Berkeley values the family needs of faculty, including dual career couples, single parents, or those who may have taken time off for family reasons. For information about potential relocation to Berkeley, or career needs of accompanying partners and spouses, please visit the Office for Faculty Equity and Welfare's website . Qualifications Basic qualifications (required at time of application)
  
Completion of a doctoral degree (e.g., PhD), or equivalent international degree, or enrolled in a doctoral degree or equivalent international degree-granting program at the time of application. Preferred qualifications
  
Preference will be given to applicants interested in AI and machine learning methods development that advance the understanding of complex biological systems as well as to applicants whose research, teaching, or service has prepared them to contribute to our commitment to create, educate, and serve our society. Application Requirements Document requirements
  
  
Cover Letter
  
  
Curriculum Vitae - Your most recently updated C.V. with complete list of publications. Please list prior academic, professional and/or public service activities and future service interests. This can include, for example, participating in professional or scientific associations, serving on committees that advance department, campus or discipline goals, and conducting outreach activities that can remove barriers and increase participation of academics in your field.

This can include, for example, your publication record, awards, presentations, inclusive research practices, communication skills, and collaborations that promote the excellence of your research, and areas for future research. Please also discuss your mentoring experiences and approach. Applicants are responsible for asking their references to upload letters as part of the online application process. Apply link: https://aprecruit.berkeley.edu/JPF05560

UC Berkeley is committed to diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging in our public mission of research, teaching, and service, consistent with UC Regents Policy 4400 and University of California Academic Personnel policy ( APM 210 1-d ). These values are embedded in our Principles of Community , which reflect our passion for critical inquiry, debate, discovery and innovation, and our deep commitment to contributing to a better world. Every member of the UC Berkeley community has a role in sustaining a safe, caring and humane environment in which these values can thrive.

jobs.description:
The mission of the University of St. Augustine for Health Sciences is the development of professional health care practitioners through innovation, individualized, and quality classroom, clinical, and distance education.
  
  
**General Summary**
The University of St. Augustine for Health Sciences (USAHS) seeks a dynamic, innovative faculty member for a full-time Core Faculty position in the nursing programs. Responsibilities will include teaching activities primarily in one or more of the following: Master of Science in Nursing program, the Family Nurse Practice role specialty courses, Psych Mental Health specialty courses and the Doctor of Nurse Practice program.
  
  
**Essential Duties And Responsibilities**
**Teaching**

* Effectively and proficiently using online technology and resources including providing informed feedback and critique in a thoughtful, well-written and timely manner.
* Optimizing the online environment to be conducive to student learning by developing creative, challenging, and evidence-based learning opportunities.
* Uses learning assessment information to improve teaching and curriculum; participates in quality improvement initiatives to meet program and institutional goals.
* Adheres to all USAHS faculty expectations, which are clearly set forth to the faculty member at the start of his/her employment with the University.
* Upholds the expectations of masters/doctoral level work with respect to the program and course learning outcomes.
* Participates in a culture of assessment of academic integrity, effectiveness and doctoral quality teaching and learning.
* Teaches three to four assigned courses/sections per trimester in accordance with the faculty expectations and as outlined in the USAHS employee handbook.
* Effectively supervises scholarly projects and practicum experiences
* Participate in residency experiences as assigned (may require travel).

**Scholarship**

* Establishes and implements an approved scholarship plan/faculty development plan as required by accreditation and university standards.
* Stays current with clinical practice and evidence that support content area expertise, professional growth, and professional certification and licensure requirements.
* Disseminates scholarly work consistent with University policies and accreditation expectations.
* Demonstrates commitment to scholarly advancement through research, written artifacts, scholarly inquiry and presentations at state, national and international professional events (minimum one per year).

**Service**

* Serves on programmatic and university committees as assigned.
* Actively participates in his/her professional association(s).
* Serves as university liaison in community and/or professional activities.
* Uses release time that enhances the program (e.g., clinical practice, consultation, advanced degree attainment, research, service) as approved by the program director.
* Participates in university governance, curriculum planning, and functions to support development and growth of the institution.
* Participates in a minimum of two to three committees (depending on requirements) and attends all university functions as assigned.

**Administration: supports efficient and consistent practices across all programs**

* Performs course coordinator and lead instructor roles as assigned; works collaboratively with members of the team.
* Advises students on academic, professional and/or personal issues while providing referrals when appropriate.
* Provides other administrative duties as assigned.
* Completes annual self-evaluation of faculty performance and sets goals for the next year in collaboration with the program director and is actively engaged in faculty development opportunities to meet performance goals.

**Professionalism: displays the behaviors of a professional academician and follows expected discipline specific Code of Ethics**

* Promotes professionalism by modeling and encouraging such behaviors inside and outside the classroom setting.
* Supports and exemplifies the University’s core values.
* Actively engages in interprofessional collaboration activities.
* Upholds and enforces student and faculty handbook policies and University policies/procedures.

**Other Responsibilities As Assigned By The Program Director**
**BUSINESS COMPETENCIES**
To perform the job successfully, an individual should demonstrate the following competencies:
  
  

* Committed to Mission and Values - Has a clear understanding of institution’s mission and values. Has a passion for facilitating learning and for enabling students to navigate their own learning journey.
* Contribute Knowledge to the Discipline - Compelled by the opportunity to contribute through research, scholarship professional practice or creativity.
* Accountable -Takes personal responsibility for own goals and outcomes to ensure student success. Establishes clear expectations, follows through on commitments to students and holds them accountable for assignments and performance
* Collaborative - Works cooperatively with others across the institution and beyond, including the community and through partnerships. Represents own interests while being inclusive and fair to others.
* Communicates Effectively - Adapts oral and written communication approach and style to the audience and based on the message. Also listens attentively to others.
* Drives Engagement - Makes students feel welcome, understood and valued. Creates a learning environment that is compelling, challenging and productive.
* Academic Discipline Expertise - Has sufficient credentials, industry expertise and/or experience in the discipline to teach according to the standards and qualifications required.
* Education Design - Designs learning experiences closely linked to learning outcomes including lesson planning, design of project, work integrated, group learning experiences, or interactive learning objects. Has depth of expertise in pedagogy, andragogy and overall learning effectiveness.
* Teaching Delivery/Learning Facilitation Skills - Manages small, large, blended, hybrid and/or online classrooms, monitoring and ensuring participation, managing oneï¿½s own and studentsï¿½ time and attention effectively.

**Additional Competencies**

* Utilizes an engaged, proactive and responsive style in communicating with students and colleagues as well as participation in research and university service.
* Demonstrates the ability to encourage critical thinking, helping students see multiple viewpoints, encouraging them along a path of continual improvement, and keeps up to date with developments in teaching and learning.
* Responds in a constructive, detailed and timely manner. Provides open-minded and receptive responses to student inquiry.
* Sets expectations with students about assignments and evaluates work products against stated expectations. Assesses students' critical thinking skills and writing skills in addition to content mastery.
* Utilizes clarity and specificity about how students' scholarly work will be evaluated. Informs students of their academic progress in meeting course expectations by regularly providing grades and feedback. Provides timely and substantive feedback in the gradebook and other appropriate places. Grades assignments consistently using rubrics.
* Adheres to the highest ethical standards and scholarly codes in practicing academic freedom. Respects the privacy of students and protecting the intellectual property of others that might be infringed upon through copyright violation or plagiarism.
* Effectively directs instruction and mentoring roles toward preparing students as agents of social change.
* Integrates various forms of scholarship into professional activities enabling creation of create new knowledge through research, interpretation of knowledge across disciplines, examination of teaching models to achieve optimal learning, and progress toward solution of problems within the profession and across society.
* Maintains an inter-professional focus, demonstrating respect and collaboration for all members of the healthcare team.
* Considers cultural and ethical aspects of teaching, learning and administrative duties.
* Supports a healthy organization by developing trust, mutual respect and honesty during all interactions.
* Exhibits excellent organization and time management skills.
* Follows through on commitments and is accountable for actions and outcomes.
* Maintains a working knowledge of educational theory and methodology.
* Establishes and maintains computer literacy including all features of Microsoft Office.

**LICENSING / CERTIFICATION**
Faculty members must be appropriately credentialed, possess an earned degree from an accredited institution, and expected to be licensed as a Registered Nurse and/or Advanced Practice Registered Nurse (if applicable). Faculty members must maintain their license(s) and any appropriate certifications in order to continue to teach at University of Saint Augustine for Health Sciences. Faculty members may be asked to seek additional state licenses if required. Faculty members are also expected to maintain currency with nursing practice and education by reviewing articles, journals, and presentations. If participating in research, the Faculty member may publish and acknowledge University of Saint Augustine for Health Sciences.
  
  
**TRAVEL**
Some travel may be required for residencies, faculty meetings or immersions.
  
  
**EDUCATION And/or EXPERIENCE**

* A terminal degree in nursing (PhD or DNP)
* Active and unencumbered RN license in home state and eligible for licensure in all 50 states
* Current national certification as a Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP)
* APRN license in home state as well as states where students live, if required.
* A significant record of intellectual and professional contributions to the field of nursing, including experience in the practice of education and nursing.
* Teaching experience is required; teaching at doctoral level of the program is preferred. Rank is determined at point of hire based on years of teaching experience, publications, scholarship, and committee work.
* Experience in teaching advanced practice nursing, especially in PMHNP role, is required if assigned to PMHNP coursework.
* Experience with distance learning preferred.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT**
Work is performed primarily in a standard office environment but may involve exposure to moderate noise levels. Work involves operation of personal computer equipment for six to eight hours daily and includes physical demands associated with a traditional office setting, e.g., walking, standing, communicating, and other physical functions as necessary.
  
  
Hiring ranges:
  
  

* Affiliated/Instructor rank: $59,758 - $100,394
* Assistant Professor rank: $68,722 – $115,400
* Associate Professor rank: $79,030 - $132,710
* Professor rank: $88,923 - $152,617

**Position Title:**

Assistant / Associate / Professor of Elementary Education

**Compensation:**

$70,000 - $95,000

**Department:**

Elementary Education

08/02/2027

**About this opportunity:**

Ball State University’s Department of Elementary Education invites applications for a full-time, tenure-line faculty position at the Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor rank beginning August 2027. While candidates at all ranks will be considered, we are particularly interested in applicants whose experiences and accomplishments support appointment at the Associate or Full Professor level.
  
  
Salary range for Assistant Professor: $70,000 - $75,000  
Salary range for Associate Professor or Professor: $75,000 - $95,000
  
  
We seek a collaborative teacher-scholar committed to preparing highly effective elementary educators and advancing knowledge in teaching and learning. The successful candidate will contribute to undergraduate and graduate programs in elementary education, with particular emphasis on literacy, inclusive teaching practices, and curriculum and instruction. We are especially interested in candidates whose teaching, scholarship, and professional engagement reflect current research and evidence-based practices in elementary education and who can contribute leadership to the department’s teaching, research, partnerships, and program development.
  
  
This position offers opportunities to teach and mentor undergraduate and graduate students, supervise candidates in field-based settings, maintain a productive program of research and scholarship, collaborate with faculty and school/community partners, and contribute to the ongoing development of innovative educator preparation programs. Candidates at the Associate or Full Professor level should demonstrate a sustained record of scholarly productivity and professional contributions appropriate to rank.
  
  
Employer will consider sponsorship.

Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in elementary education, with particular emphasis on literacy, inclusive teaching practices, and curriculum and instruction; supervise practicum and other field-based experiences; establish and maintain an active program of research and scholarly publication; pursue opportunities for external funding as appropriate; engage in partnerships with schools, families, communities, and other educational organizations; advise and mentor graduate students, including doctoral students; collaborate with faculty on program development and improvement; provide leadership appropriate to experience and rank; and provide professional university, college, and departmental service.

Salary range for Assistant Professor: $70,000 - $75,000  
Salary range for Associate Professor or Professor: $75,000 - $95,000

* Demonstrated record of scholarly productivity, as evidenced by refereed presentations at regional, national, or international conferences and/or scholarly publications such as refereed journal articles, book chapters, or books.

* Knowledge of, and experience with, using current approaches to inclusive teaching, culturally responsive and sustaining pedagogies, and/or equitable educational practice while teaching learners with a wide range of strengths, needs, experiences, and backgrounds
* Experience supervising preservice teachers or other educator candidates in field-based settings.
* Demonstrated commitment to and experience with partnerships involving schools, families, communities, and/or community agencies.
* Record of seeking and/or obtaining external grant funding.
* Experience effectively integrating educational technologies into teaching, including online or technology-enhanced instruction.
* Evidence of effective collaboration with colleagues and other educational partners.
* For candidates at the Associate or Full Professor level, evidence of leadership in one or more areas such as program development, curriculum innovation, graduate education, research initiatives, externally funded projects, professional organizations, or school and community partnerships.
* Experience mentoring graduate students, doctoral students, and/or early-career faculty
* A sustained record of scholarly productivity and professional engagement appropriate to rank.

ELED Department Chairperson, Jackie Sydnor jtsydnor@bsu.edu

---------------------

The Department of Mathematics at Colorado State University invites applications for one tenure-track assistant professor position in the area of Applied and Computational Mathematics with an anticipated start date of August 16, 2027. A broad range of application areas will be considered. Candidates should have an established research program, a compelling plan for future research, the ability to supervise both graduate and undergraduate research, and a record of excellence in teaching. The salary is competitive and commensurate with qualifications and experience, and includes a full benefits package.

  

The Department of Mathematics at Colorado State University is one of eight departments in the College of Natural Sciences. Faculty research interests include algebra, analysis, combinatorics, differential equations, geometry, inverse problems, math education, mathematical modeling, number theory, scientific computing, and topology, as well as applications of these areas. jobs.description:
**Job Description**
THIS POSITION IS LOCATED IN NASHVILLE, TN
  
  
The University of Tennessee Health Sciences Department of General Dentistry seeks a part-time non-tenure Open Rank Professor (60-80% FTE). This position plays a pivotal role in the UT Health Sciences College of Dentistry, contributing to the education, clinical training, and professional development of dental students. This faculty member will be actively engaged across multiple sub-departments, including Advanced Education in General Dentistry (AEGD) and General Dentistry, ensuring a well-rounded learning experience for residents.
  
  
**Responsibilities**
**TEACHING AND CURRICULUM DEVELOPMENT:**

* Deliver didactic, post-doc, and clinical instruction in General Dentistry, ensuring residents advance competency in evidence-based practices.
* Develop and implement innovative teaching strategies to enhance student engagement and learning outcomes.

**Clinical Supervision And Patient Care**

* Provide hands-on clinical training, guiding students in diagnostic, preventive, and restorative procedures.
* Supervise students ensuring adherence to best practices in patient care.
* Clinical oversight and mentorship.
* Contribute to patient care and clinical research initiatives.
* Provide mentorship to residents within the Advanced Education in General Dentistry Program.

**Interdisciplinary Collaboration And Institutional Service**

* Work closely with faculty across various dental disciplines to integrate interdisciplinary approaches into resident education.
* Participate in faculty committees, accreditation processes, and strategic planning initiatives to support institutional goals.
* Engage in community outreach programs, promoting oral health education and access to care.

**Research And Scholarly Activities**

* Contribute to departmental research, supporting advancements in General Dentistry techniques and education.
* Mentor students, residents, and junior faculty in research projects, publications, and presentations.
* Stay updated on emerging trends and technologies in dentistry, integrating them into teaching and clinical practice.

**Qualifications**
**EDUCATION:**
DDS/DMD or equivalent degree.
  
  
**LICENSES:**
Eligibility for a Tennessee Dental License or a teaching license.
  
  
**Departmental Preferences**

* Experience in private practice or advanced graduate training in General Dentistry.
* Prior teaching experience preferred but not required.
* Proficiency in electronic health records and contemporary dental techniques.
* Strong communication and organizational skills.
* Strong interpersonal skills to effectively interact with others.
* Ability to adapt to interdisciplinary collaboration and clinical environment.

**THE UNIVERSITY OF TENNESSEE HEALTH SCIENCES**
The University of Tennessee Health Sciences is a statewide flagship, public, academic health institution in Tennessee. Founded in 1911, the mission of the University of Tennessee Health Sciences is to improve the health and well-being of Tennesseans and the global community by fostering collaborative education, research, scientific discovery, clinical care, and public service. Employing more than 4,600 people on its faculty, staff, and not-for-profit corporation faculty practice groups, and with more than 3,200 students across the state, UT Health Sciences contributes $4 billion to the economy of Tennessee.
  
  
Part of the University of Tennessee System, the Health Sciences is headquartered in Memphis and includes all six of UT’s doctoral-degree-granting health science colleges -- Medicine, Dentistry, Pharmacy, Nursing, Graduate Health Sciences, and Health Professions. UT Health Sciences spans the state with its four major, regional clinical health science locations in Memphis, Knoxville, Chattanooga, and Nashville, as well as more than 100 clinical education sites across Tennessee. UT Health Sciences is the largest educator of health care professionals in the state and operates the state’s largest residency and fellowship advanced training programs.
  
  
Located in West Tennessee on the banks of the Mississippi River, Memphis is the second-largest city in the state and among the largest cities in the Southeast. The Greater Memphis metropolitan area has more than 1.3 million residents, and the city ranks among those with the lowest cost of living in the country. It is home to a vibrant restaurant scene, a revitalized Downtown, the Midtown Arts District, many scenic neighborhoods, an active medical district, and a burgeoning airport in the midst of a $214 million modernization.
  
  
Memphis boasts attractions, including Elvis Presley’s Graceland, the Memphis Grizzlies, historic Beale Street, the National Civil Rights Museum, the second-largest urban county park in the United States, and the Memphis in May World Championship Barbecue Cooking Contest.
